definition_zh: 安排；筹备；排列；布局；协议；改编曲
definition_en: the act of planning or laying out something, the resulting order, an agreement, or a piece of music adapted for performance
core_image: 一张写满备注的流程表，每件事都已排进自己的格子
scene: 婚礼前夜，长桌上摊着一张写满时间与座位的流程表，负责人正逐项核对。 Every arrangement had been written down and checked twice.
sceneCN: 这里 arrangement 是「安排、筹备」（第 1 个义项：为某件事所做的准备与计划）；句意为「每一项安排都已写下并核对了两遍」。画面中有流程表、铅笔与长桌。

pos.zh: 名词：安排；筹备；排列；布局；协议；改编曲

derivatives.zh: arrangement 的动词形式，义为「安排；整理；商定；改编」
由 arrange 加 -er 构成，义为「安排者；乐曲改编者」
由前缀 re- 加 arrange 构成，义为「重新安排」

senses.title: The act of planning and preparing
senses.definition: the act of planning and organizing something, or the plans that result from it
senses.definitionCN: 计划并组织某件事的行为，或由此形成的计划
senses.example: The travel agency made all the arrangements for us.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行社为我们做好了一切安排。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns the verb into the thing done: the rows that have been set.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词变成「做完的事」：那些已经排好的行。

senses.title: The way things are laid out
senses.definition: the order or pattern in which objects or elements are placed
senses.definitionCN: 物件或元素被摆放时所形成的顺序与样式
senses.example: The seating arrangement put the two old friends side by side.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的座位安排让两位老朋友坐在了一起。
senses.why: Here the noun names the row itself, seen as a finished shape rather than an action.
senses.whyCN: 这里的名词指「排好的行」本身，被看成完成的形状，而不是一次动作。

senses.title: An agreement between parties
senses.definition: an agreement or understanding reached with another person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或团体达成的协议或谅解
senses.example: They reached an arrangement with the landlord about the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他们与房东就租金达成了约定。
senses.why: Two parties are two rows of terms; when both line up, the arrangement exists.
senses.whyCN: 双方就是两排条款；两边对齐时，协议便成立了。

senses.title: A piece of music adapted for performance
senses.definition: a version of a piece of music rewritten for particular instruments, voices, or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 为特定乐器、人声或演出而改写的乐曲版本
senses.example: The orchestra played a jazz arrangement of the old waltz.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团演奏了那首老华尔兹的爵士改编版。
senses.why: The notes were rowed anew, so the noun names the score that came out of that reordering.
senses.whyCN: 音符被重新排过一遍，于是名词指重新排列后产生的乐谱。

intro.en: Arrangement is the noun built on arrange, and it inherits the same row image from a Germanic root by way of French.
intro.cn: arrangement 是建立在 arrange 之上的名词，经由法语承袭了同一个来自日耳曼词根的「排成行」意象。

items.en: 「*hringaz」 is reconstructed as 'ring, circle', the shape word behind the French root rang.
items.cn: 「*hringaz」被重构为「环、圈」，它是法语词根 rang 背后的形状词。

items.en: Frankish 「*hring」 kept the ring sense, but the shift from circle to row is source uncertain.
items.cn: 法兰克语「*hring」保留「环」义，但从圆圈到一排的转变来源存疑。

items.en: Arengier meant 'to put in a row'; its noun arengement named the resulting order.
items.cn: arengier 意为「排成行」，其名词 arengement 指排好后的次序。

items.en: Arranger and its noun carried the word into the senses of preparing and agreeing.
items.cn: arranger 及其名词把这个词带入「筹备」与「达成一致」的义域。

items.en: English took the noun in the fifteenth century, keeping both the physical and the planning senses.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，物理排列与计划筹备两义同时保留。

items.en: The musical sense is the latest: a score that has been set in a new order.
items.cn: 音乐义最晚出现：一份被重新排过次序的乐谱。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns that resemble arrangement in form; the near-meaning group gathers plans, layouts, deals and preparations.
note.cn: 形近组收形式上与 arrangement 相近的名词；近义组收计划、布局、协议与准备工作。

entries.definition: The legal act of bringing someone before a court to answer a charge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「传讯、提审」，指带某人到法庭应讯的法律程序。

entries.definition: The state of being in a straight line or in correct relation to something else.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「对齐、一致」，指排成直线或与他物关系正确。

entries.definition: The activity of running an organization, or the people who run it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理」或「管理层」。

entries.definition: A set of steps worked out in advance for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而预先拟定的步骤。

entries.definition: The way items are arranged on a page or in a space.
entries.definitionCN: 物件在页面或空间中的摆放方式。

entries.definition: An agreement, especially in business or politics.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指商业或政治上的协议。

entries.definition: The work of getting something ready.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事准备就绪的工作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow arrangement from a written plan to a seating chart, a deal and a score.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子让 arrangement 从书面计划走到座位表、协议与乐谱。

normal.en: Arrangement is the row already finished.
normal.cn: arrangement 是已经排好的那一行。

normal.en: Make arrangements: the plans sit in their boxes.
normal.cn: 做出安排：计划各自落在格子里。

normal.en: Seating arrangement: people become rows on a chart.
normal.cn: 座位安排：人在图表上排成行。

normal.en: An arrangement with a bank is a row of agreed terms.
normal.cn: 与银行的协议就是一排谈妥的条款。

normal.en: A jazz arrangement is notes set in a new row.
normal.cn: 爵士改编曲就是重新排过行的音符。

abstract.en: A noun can name both the act and the finished order.
abstract.cn: 一个名词既能指动作，也能指完成后的次序。

abstract.en: The same word settles objects, people and music.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能安顿物件、人与人之间的关系，以及音乐。

abstract.en: Every sense is a row that someone has made.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是某个人排出来的一行。

examples.en: The travel agency made all the arrangements for us.
examples.cn: 旅行社为我们做好了一切安排。

examples.en: The seating arrangement put the two old friends side by side.
examples.cn: 这样的座位安排让两位老朋友坐在了一起。

examples.en: They reached an arrangement with the landlord about the rent.
examples.cn: 他们与房东就租金达成了约定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿让门」——阿让把门口的一切安排写在纸上：安排、布局

root: arrangement 是 arrange 加名词后缀 -ment，字面就是「排成行这件事」。arrange 经由古法语 arengier 进入英语，词根 rang 意为「一排、一列」。于是这个名词既指安排与筹备的行动，也指排好后的布局、双方谈成的协议，以及把音符重排而成的改编曲。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses branch from one finished row: the act of planning, the resulting layout, an agreed set of terms, and a score set in a new order.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从一条排好的行分出来：计划的行动、形成的布局、谈妥的条款，以及重新排序的乐谱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flow chart on a long table, every item sitting in its own box.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌上的流程表，每件事都待在自己的格子里。

branches.en: THE PLAN LINE: preparation is the row made before the event.
branches.cn: 计划线：筹备就是活动之前先排好的那一行。

branches.en: THE LAYOUT LINE: the noun names the shape that the row leaves behind.
branches.cn: 布局线：名词指这一行留下的形状。

branches.en: THE DEAL LINE: two parties settle when their terms line up.
branches.cn: 协议线：双方的条件对齐时，事情就谈成了。

branches.en: THE SCORE LINE: the notes are rowed again for new performers.
branches.cn: 乐谱线：音符为新演奏者重新排过。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: a tidy room and a booked trip are both arrangements.
branches.cn: 日常线：整洁的房间与订好的行程，都是 arrangement。

intro.en: Arrangement is a verb plus the noun suffix -ment, and its family grows by adding prefixes and further suffixes.
intro.cn: arrangement 是动词加名词后缀 -ment，它的词族靠加前缀与再加后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: The root is Frankish, not Latin, so there is no Latin family to list here.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自法兰克语而非拉丁语，因此这里没有拉丁词族可列。

items.example: The arrangements were all confirmed by phone.

items.example: The prearrangement saved the guests a long wait.

scene: 体育馆的记分牌一直亮到深夜。 The championship drew teams from every province.
sceneCN: 这里 championship 指「锦标赛」（第 1 个义项：决定冠军归属的比赛）；句意是这项锦标赛吸引了各省的队伍。

pos.zh: 锦标赛；冠军称号；冠军地位

derivatives.zh: 冠军；拥护者
冠军（口语）

senses.title: A contest for the top title
senses.definition: a competition held to decide which player or team is the best
senses.definitionCN: 为决出最佳选手或队伍而举办的比赛
senses.example: The national championship starts on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 全国锦标赛周一开始。
senses.why: The suffix -ship turns the winner's name into the contest that produces a winner.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 把胜者的名字变成产出胜者的那场比赛。

senses.title: The status of being champion
senses.definition: the position or title of being a champion

senses.example: She held the championship for five years.

senses.why: The same suffix also names a state or rank, so the word can mean the title itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也能表示状态或等级，因此这个词也可指头衔本身。

definition_zh: 参与；参加；分享（收益、成本）；持有份额；（古旧）具有某种性质
definition_en: to take part in an activity or share in something with others; in older usage, to have a quality in common with something
core_image: 一只手伸进共同的事务里，并从中分到属于自己的一份
scene: 社区花园里，居民卷起袖子一起翻土、分种子、抬水桶。 Everyone who came to the garden was asked to participate, and at the end each helper took home a basket of vegetables.
sceneCN: 这里 participate 是「参与活动」（第 1 个义项：参加一项活动）；句意：每个来花园的人都被邀请参与，最后每位帮手都带回家一篮蔬菜。图中可辨识物件：铁锹、种子袋、水桶、菜畦、收成篮；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: （古旧、正式）具有；带有（某种性质）

derivatives.zh: 参与；参加
参与者；参加者
参与式的；让人参与的
参与性的（多指管理风格）
不参与的；不参加分红的

senses.title: Take part in an activity
senses.definition: to take part in an event, activity, or process with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起参加某项事件、活动或过程
senses.example: More than fifty students participated in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 五十多名学生参加了这项调查。
senses.why: Latin particeps means 'taking a part', from pars 'part' plus capere 'to take'. To participate is literally to take a part for oneself in something larger, which is why the verb always needs a whole to enter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 particeps 意为“拿取一份”，由 pars“部分”加 capere“拿取”构成。participate 字面就是“在一个更大的事情里为自己拿一份”，因此这个动词总需要一个可进入的整体。

senses.title: Take part actively: put yourself in
senses.definition: to involve oneself actively rather than merely being present
senses.definitionCN: 主动投入，而不只是身在现场
senses.example: She participated eagerly in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 她热切地参与了辩论。
senses.why: Taking a part is an action, not a seat. The word therefore implies effort: the participant reaches into the activity, while a spectator only watches it.
senses.whyCN: “拿一份”是动作，不是占个座位。因此这个词隐含付出：参与者把手伸进活动中，而旁观者只是看着。

senses.title: Share in the results
senses.definition: to share in profits, costs, or benefits with others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人分享利润、成本或收益
senses.example: The workers participate in the profits of the cooperative.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们分享合作社的利润。
senses.why: The 'part' taken can be a share of the outcome rather than a role in the work. English extends the word from joining an activity to receiving a portion of what the activity produces.
senses.whyCN: 所拿的“一份”可以是成果中的份额，而不只是工作中的一个角色。英语把这个词从“加入活动”扩展到“分得活动产出的一部分”。

senses.title: Hold a share: participating policies
senses.definition: in finance and insurance, to have a right to a share of profits or assets
senses.definitionCN: 在金融与保险中，拥有分得利润或资产的权利
senses.example: The policy is participating, so it receives annual dividends.
senses.exampleCN: 这是分红型保单，因此每年获得红利。
senses.why: Once a share can be owned, participation becomes a property right written into a contract. The word moves from doing to holding, but the underlying image is still a portion set aside for the holder.
senses.whyCN: 当“一份”可以被拥有，参与就变成写进合同的财产权。这个词从“做事”转到“持有”，但底层画面仍是为持有者留出的那一份。

senses.title: Take part in decisions
senses.definition: to have a voice or a role in making decisions that affect a group
senses.definitionCN: 在影响群体的决策中有发言权或一份作用
senses.example: Employees participate in decisions about working hours.
senses.exampleCN: 员工参与有关工时的决策。
senses.why: Decision-making is an activity with roles inside it. To participate is to hold one of those roles, which is why the word appears in arguments about democracy and workplace governance.
senses.whyCN: 决策是一项内部有角色的活动。参与就是持有其中一个角色，因此这个词会出现在关于民主与工作场所治理的讨论中。

senses.title: Enter a competition
senses.definition: to compete or take part in a contest, tournament, or exhibition
senses.definitionCN: 参加比赛、锦标赛或展览
senses.example: Twelve teams participated in the tournament.
senses.exampleCN: 十二支队伍参加了锦标赛。
senses.why: A contest is a structured whole with a fixed number of places. Entering it is taking one of those places, so the verb fits competitions as naturally as meetings.
senses.whyCN: 比赛是一个结构化的整体，名额固定。报名参赛就是占其中一个位置，因此这个动词用于竞赛和用于会议一样自然。

senses.title: Enrol as a research subject
senses.definition: to enrol oneself as a subject in a clinical trial or research study
senses.definitionCN: 作为受试者加入临床试验或研究
senses.example: Two hundred patients participated in the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 两百名患者参加了这项试验。
senses.why: In a trial the participant contributes data rather than labour. The word still means taking a part, but the part is now a measured role inside a protocol, and ethics rules grow around it.
senses.whyCN: 在试验中，参与者贡献的是数据而不是劳动。这个词仍表示“拿一份”，但这一份现在是研究方案里被测量的角色，伦理规范也随之围绕它生长。

senses.title: Have a quality in common (archaic)
senses.titleCN: 具有某种性质（古旧用法）
senses.definition: in older usage with of, to have a quality or nature in common with something
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法，与 of 连用，表示与某物共有某种性质或本性
senses.example: The essay participates of the nature of a confession.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章带有自白的性质。
senses.why: In scholastic language, sharing a quality was treated as having a share in a form. The construction participate of is a fossil of that metaphysics, which is why it now sounds literary and old.
senses.whyCN: 在经院哲学语言里，“共有一项性质”被理解为“分有一个形式”。participate of 这一结构就是那套形而上学的化石，因此今天听来既文学又古旧。

intro.en: Participate is a Latin verb built from 'part' and 'take'. Its English life began as a back-formation, and the two halves are well documented.
intro.cn: participate 是一个由“部分”与“拿取”构成的拉丁动词。它在英语中的生命始于逆构，两个成分都有明确记载。

items.en: The English verb is recorded, probably a back-formation from participation or taken directly from Latin participatus, the past participle of participare.
items.cn: 英语动词记录于 16 世纪 30 年代，很可能是从 participation 逆构而来，或直接取自拉丁语 participare 的过去分词 participatus。

items.en: Participare 'to share, take part' comes from particeps 'sharing, taking part'. Particeps joins pars 'part' with the -cip- element of capere 'to take, seize'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 participare“分享、参加”来自 particeps“分享的、参加的”。particeps 把 pars“部分”与 capere“拿取、抓住”的 -cip- 成分结合起来。

items.en: Pars goes back to PIE *pere- 'to grant, allot', the family of portion and parcel. Capere goes back to *kap- 'to grasp', the family of capture and accept. The asterisks mark reconstructed roots.
items.cn: pars 上溯原始印欧语 *pere-“给予、分配”，是 portion 与 parcel 的词族。capere 上溯 *kap-“抓取”，是 capture 与 accept 的词族。星号表示重构词根。

items.en: The construction participate of appears, meaning 'to have a quality in common with'. It belongs to scholastic talk of sharing in a form and is now archaic.
items.cn: participate of 这一结构出现于 16 世纪 60 年代，意为“与……共有某种性质”。它属于经院哲学关于“分有形式”的说法，如今已属古旧。

items.en: Finance and insurance extend the word to profit-sharing: participating policy, participating shares. Twentieth-century institutions add participatory democracy and clinical trial participation.
items.cn: 金融与保险把词扩展到利润分享：分红型保单、参与分红的股份。20 世纪的制度又添上“参与式民主”与“临床试验参与”。

note.en: The first group is built on the same part- root but means something else; the second compares verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组同样带 part- 词根但意思不同；第二组比较表示“加入”的动词。

entries.definition: a verb form used as an adjective, such as broken or running. It comes from Latin participium 'a sharing', so it is a relative of participate but not a form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用作形容词的动词形式，如 broken 或 running。它来自拉丁语 participium“分享”，因而是 participate 的亲戚，却不是它的词形变化。

entries.definition: a person who takes part. It is the noun from participate, not a separate verb.
entries.definitionCN: 参与者。它是 participate 派生的名词，不是另一个动词。

entries.definition: the act of taking part. The -ion suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的行为。-ion 后缀把动词变成动作名词。

entries.definition: concerning only a part; biased. It shares the pars root but has no capere element and does not mean taking part.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的；偏袒的。它共享 pars 词根，但没有 capere 成分，也不表示“参加”。

entries.definition: to be present at an event. It stresses presence, while participate stresses contributing or sharing.
entries.definitionCN: 出席某个活动。它强调在场，而 participate 强调贡献或分享。

entries.definition: to become a member of a group or activity. It marks entry, while participate marks the activity once inside.
entries.definitionCN: 成为某群体或活动的一员。它标记“进入”，而 participate 标记进入之后的活动。

entries.definition: to become involved with something, often with commitment. It is broader and can be passive or hostile as well as cooperative.
entries.definitionCN: 投入某事，常含承诺。它更宽泛，既可合作，也可被动甚至对抗。

entries.definition: to give something such as effort, money, or ideas to a shared purpose. It stresses what is given, while participate stresses being one of the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目标付出努力、金钱或想法。它强调“给出什么”，而 participate 强调“成为其中一份”。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on part + take, then three abstract images about shares and belonging.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 part + take 的挂钩，再用三个关于“份额与归属”的抽象画面。

normal.en: Split it: parti- is part, -cip- is take (as in capture). Participate = take a part.
normal.cn: 拆开看：parti- 是“部分”，-cip- 是“拿取”（如 capture）。participate＝拿一份。

normal.en: participate in, not participate at: you enter a whole, so the preposition is in.
normal.cn: 是 participate in，不是 participate at：你进入的是一个整体，所以介词用 in。

normal.en: A participant is one who took a part; the -ant ending marks the person holding the share.
normal.cn: participant 就是“拿了那一份的人”；-ant 结尾标记持有这份的人。

normal.en: In a meeting, presence is attendance; speaking is participation. Two different words for two different levels.
normal.cn: 在会上，到场是 attendance，发言才是 participation。两个词对应两个层次。

normal.en: A participating policy pays you a part of the profits; the same 'share' idea, now in money.
normal.cn: 分红型保单（participating policy）把一部分利润分给你；还是“一份”的意思，只是换成了钱。

abstract.en: To participate is to accept a share of both the work and the consequence; the two cannot be separated.
abstract.cn: 参与就是同时接受工作与后果中的一份；这两者无法分开。

abstract.en: A whole is made of parts that agreed to be counted. Participation is the act of being counted.
abstract.cn: 整体由同意被计入的部分组成。参与就是让自己被计入的动作。

abstract.en: The older sense reminds us that things can share a nature, not only a task: participation began as metaphysics before it became management.
abstract.cn: 古旧义提醒我们：事物不仅能共担任务，也能共有本性——参与先是一种形而上学，然后才成为管理术语。

examples.en: All staff are encouraged to participate in the safety review.
examples.cn: 鼓励全体员工参与安全审查。

examples.en: The company participates in a pension scheme for every employee.
examples.cn: 公司为每位员工参加了一项养老金计划。

examples.en: She participated of a stubbornness that ran in the family.
examples.cn: 她身上带有这个家族遗传的固执。

dict_mnemonic.note: parti- 记成“部分”，-cip- 记成“拿”（capere）：伸手拿一份，就是参与。
dict_mnemonic.text: parti（部分）+ cip（拿取）+ -ate（动词）→ 拿一份 → 参与、分享

root: 拉丁 particeps“分享的、参与的”＝pars“部分”（原始印欧语 *pere-“分配”）+ -cip-（capere“拿取”，*kap-）→ participare → participate。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from taking a part in an activity, to taking it actively, to sharing the results, holding a financial share, joining decisions, entering a contest, enrolling in a trial, and finally the old metaphysical sense of sharing a quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“在活动中拿一份”开始，转到积极投入、分享成果、持有金融份额、参与决策、报名参赛、加入试验，最后落到古旧的形而上学义：共有一项性质。

core.en: A hand reaching into a shared task and coming away with its own portion
core.cn: 一只手伸进共同的事务，并从中取走属于自己的那一份

chain: HAVE A SHARE OF A QUALITY

branches.en: Entering structured wholes: an activity, a survey, or a tournament with limited places.
branches.cn: 进入结构化的整体：活动、调查，或名额有限的比赛。

branches.en: From effort to voice: active involvement, and a role in deciding.
branches.cn: 从出力到发声：积极投入，以及在决策中的一份角色。

branches.en: The share as income: profit-sharing, and a contractual right to dividends.
branches.cn: 作为收入的份额：分享利润，以及合同上的分红权。

branches.en: The measured role: a trial subject is still taking part, but inside a protocol.
branches.cn: 被测量的角色：受试者仍在“参加”，只是身处研究方案之中。

branches.en: The old sense: to have a quality in common with something, used with of.
branches.cn: 古旧义：与某物共有某种性质，常与 of 连用。

intro.en: Participate belongs to the part- family and the capere family. The derivatives below show the person, the act, the adjective of style, and the financial participle.
intro.cn: participate 属于 part- 词族，也属于 capere 词族。下面的派生词展示了人、行为、风格形容词，以及金融用法中的分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin participare and particeps are the direct sources. Pars gives the 'part', capere gives the 'take'; both are old Latin words with reconstructed PIE roots.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 participare 与 particeps 是直接来源。pars 提供“部分”，capere 提供“拿取”；两者都是古老拉丁词，有重构的原始印欧语词根。

items.meaning: to take part or share in something

items.exampleCN: 每位参与者都收到一份表格。

items.meaning: organized so that people can take part
items.example: The project uses a participatory method.
items.exampleCN: 该项目采用参与式方法。

items.meaning: allowing or encouraging involvement, especially in management
items.meaningCN: 参与性的，尤指管理风格

items.meaning: not taking part; not sharing in profits
items.exampleCN: 不参与分红的股份没有红利。

items.example: Each part has its own function.
items.exampleCN: 每一部分都有自己的功能。

items.example: The verb captures the idea of taking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词抓住了“拿取”的意思。

items.meaning: taking part; in insurance, sharing in profits

latinEntries.meaning: to share, to take part in
latinEntries.example: Participare is the direct source of English participate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: participare 是英语 participate 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Particeps literally means taking a part.
latinEntries.exampleCN: particeps 字面意为“拿取一份”。

latinEntries.meaning: a part, a portion, a share
latinEntries.example: Pars is the base of portion and partial.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pars 是 portion 与 partial 的基础。
participatio 是英语 participation 的基础。

definition_zh: 尤其；显著地；值得注意的是
definition_en: especially, or in a way that is easy to notice
core_image: 一群人中只有一个人穿亮色外套，视线自然落在他身上
scene: 报告在列举增长地区时，特别点出了一个省。 Several provinces grew, notably the coastal one.
sceneCN: 这里指从一组中特别举出一项（第 3 个义项：举出突出例子）；句意为几个省都有增长，尤其是沿海那个省；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 尤其；显著地；值得注意的是

derivatives.zh: 显著的；值得注意的

senses.title: Especially
senses.definition: more than others, in a way that deserves attention
senses.definitionCN: 比其余更突出，值得注意
senses.example: The region is notably dry in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区夏季格外干燥。
senses.why: The adverb raises one item above its neighbours without saying it is the only one.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把某一项抬到邻项之上，却不说它是唯一的一项。

senses.title: Sentence-opening highlight
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, drawing attention to the fact that follows
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，把注意力引向随后的事实
senses.example: Notably, no one objected to the change.
senses.exampleCN: 值得注意的是，没有人反对这一改动。
senses.why: The initial position tells the reader that the next clause is the point worth remembering.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置告诉读者，下一个小句才是值得记住的要点。

senses.title: Introducing a striking example
senses.definition: used before a noun phrase to single out an example
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词短语前，单举一个例子
senses.example: Some countries, notably Germany, changed their policy.
senses.exampleCN: 一些国家，尤其是德国，改变了政策。
senses.why: The word introduces a specimen that makes the general claim concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个词引出一个样本，使一般性说法变得具体。

senses.title: To a noticeable degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say a quality is easy to observe
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，表示某种性质容易观察到
senses.example: The two versions are notably different in tone.
senses.exampleCN: 两个版本在语气上明显不同。
senses.why: Here it modifies an adjective and measures visibility, close to noticeably.
senses.whyCN: 这里修饰形容词，衡量的是「可见程度」，接近「明显地」。

senses.title: Notably absent
senses.definition: in the fixed pattern notably absent, conspicuous by not being there
senses.definitionCN: 在固定搭配「显著缺席」中，指因不在场而引人注意
senses.example: Notably absent from the report was any mention of cost.
senses.exampleCN: 报告中明显缺席的是任何关于成本的提及。
senses.why: The phrase turns absence itself into the noticeable fact, a common rhetorical move.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语把「缺席」本身变成引人注意的事实，是常见的修辞手法。

senses.title: Before a comparative
senses.definition: used with a comparative to mark a difference larger than expected
senses.definitionCN: 与比较级连用，标记超出预期的差距
senses.example: This year's harvest was notably better than last year's.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的收成明显好于去年。
senses.why: With comparatives the word enlarges the gap rather than merely reporting it.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，它放大差距，而不只是报告差距。

senses.title: Academic evidence marker
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的证据标记
senses.definition: in research writing, flagging the observation that carries the argument
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中，标出支撑论证的那项观察
senses.example: The study found, notably, that older users adapted faster.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现，值得注意的是，年长用户适应得更快。
senses.why: The marker tells readers which result the author treats as decisive.
senses.whyCN: 这个标记告诉读者，作者把哪一项结果当作关键。

senses.title: In a way that attracts notice
senses.definition: of behaviour or appearance, in a manner that draws attention
senses.definitionCN: 指行为或外表以引人注意的方式
senses.example: The house was notably decorated for the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子为节日做了惹眼的装饰。
senses.why: The older manner sense describes doing something in a way that is meant to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 较早的方式义描述以「就是要被看见」的方式做事。

intro.en: Notably comes from the Latin adjective for worthy of note, through French, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「值得注意的」形容词，经法语，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun nota means a mark, sign or written note.
items.cn: 名词意为「记号、标记、注记」。

items.en: The verb notare means to mark or observe, and gives the stem of the adjective.
items.cn: 动词意为「标记、注意」，提供形容词词干。

items.en: The adjective notabilis means worthy of note or remarkable.
items.cn: 形容词意为「值得注意的、显著的」。

items.en: Old French notable and English notable carry the adjective into use.
items.cn: 古法语与英语形容词把它带入使用。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern prose uses notably both to single out examples and to measure visible degree.
items.cn: 现代散文既用它单举例子，也用它衡量可见的程度。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin mark-root; the second group contrasts highlighting an example with intensifying a degree.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「记号」词根；第二组对照「举出例子」与「加强程度」。

entries.definition: Worthy of attention; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 值得注意的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The state of being important enough to be noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 重要到足以被注意的状态。

entries.definition: A system of written marks or symbols.
entries.definitionCN: 书写的记号或符号系统。

entries.definition: To mark something with symbols or notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用符号或注记标出某物。

entries.definition: Above all, or to a high degree; broader than notably because it also intensifies.
entries.definitionCN: 首先、格外；比「值得注意的是」更宽，因为它也能单纯加强程度。

entries.definition: Specifically or especially; often narrower and more precise than especially.
entries.definitionCN: 具体地或尤其；常比「尤其」更窄、更精确。

entries.definition: In a surprising or striking degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以达到令人惊讶或醒目的程度。

entries.definition: In a way that is clearly visible or attracting attention.
entries.definitionCN: 以清楚可见或引人注意的方式。

entries.definition: A phrase singling out one member of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 从一组中单举一个成员的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real mark-root and the real split between singling out an example and measuring degree.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「记号」词根，并区分「单举例子」与「衡量程度」。

normal.en: The root is a mark, so notably points to the item with a mark beside it.
normal.cn: 词根是「记号」，所以这个词指向旁边打了记号的那一项。

normal.en: Notably absent is a sentence about what is not there, which makes the gap loud.
normal.cn: 「显著缺席」说的是不在场的东西，反而让空缺更响。

normal.en: Before a comparative it says the gap is bigger than you might assume.
normal.cn: 放在比较级前，它说明差距比你以为的更大。

normal.en: In academic prose it quietly tells the reader which result matters.
normal.cn: 在学术文字里，它悄悄告诉读者哪项结果才重要。

normal.en: Most notably often opens a list that ends with the strongest case.
normal.cn: 「最值得注意的是」常引出一个以最强例子收尾的清单。

abstract.en: A mark on a page is a promise that this part will be looked at twice.
abstract.cn: 纸上的记号是一种承诺：这一处会被再看一眼。

abstract.en: Attention is a scarce resource, and the word spends it on one item.
abstract.cn: 注意力是稀缺资源，这个词把它花在其中一项上。

abstract.en: Saying what is notably absent is a way of describing a room by its missing chair.
abstract.cn: 说某物显著缺席，就是靠少了一把椅子来描述一间屋子。

examples.en: The team improved, notably in defence.
examples.cn: 球队进步了，尤其是在防守方面。

examples.en: Notably, the two accounts disagree on the date.
examples.cn: 值得注意的是，两份记载在日期上并不一致。

examples.en: The second method is notably cheaper to run.
examples.cn: 第二种方法运行起来明显更便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诺特布利」——被特别记在备忘录上，所以显著

root: 拉丁语名词「记号」派生动词「标记、注意」，再构成形容词「值得注意的」；英语经法语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate emphasis above neighbours, sentence-opening highlight, a singled-out example, visible degree, conspicuous absence, enlarged comparison, academic evidence marking and attention-drawing manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理高于邻项的强调、句首提示、单举例子、可见程度、显著缺席、放大的比较、学术证据标记，以及引人注意的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bright coat in a crowd, pulling every glance toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群里一件亮色外套，把视线都拉过去。

branches.en: THE RAISED ITEM: one thing stands above its neighbours.
branches.cn: 被抬高的一项：某物高于邻项。

branches.en: THE FLAG: the sentence-opening highlight and the academic evidence marker.
branches.cn: 旗标：句首提示与学术证据标记。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE: a specimen that makes the general claim concrete.
branches.cn: 例子：使一般说法具体化的样本。

branches.en: THE MEASURED DEGREE: visible quality and an enlarged comparison.
branches.cn: 可测的程度：可见的性质与被放大的比较。

branches.en: THE NOTICED ABSENCE AND MANNER: the gap heard loud, and behaviour meant to be seen.
branches.cn: 被注意的空缺与方式：响亮的缺席，以及有意被看见的举止。

intro.en: Notably is a Latin mark-noun, a Latin verb stem, an adjective suffix, a French layer and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「记号」名词、「标记」动词词干、形容词后缀、法语层与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The noun for a mark builds a verb of marking and an adjective of being worth a mark, from which English takes the adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「记号」的名词构成「标记」动词与「值得被标记」的形容词，英语由它取得副词。

items.example: The noun is the concrete mark that starts the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族起点的具体记号。

items.example: The verb turns the mark into an act of noticing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把记号变成「注意到」的动作。

items.example: The suffix builds an adjective of worthiness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表「值得」的形容词。

items.example: The adjective says a thing deserves a mark beside it.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词说某物值得在旁边打个记号。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for people and events worth attention.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词，用于值得注意的人与事。

items.example: The noun names the social result of being noticed.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名被注意带来的社会结果。

items.example: A different branch of the family names written symbols.
items.exampleCN: 词族的另一支命名书写的符号。

items.example: The verb returns to the physical act of marking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词回到「做记号」的具体动作。

items.example: The suffix turns notable into a highlighting adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成提示性副词。

definition_zh: 药物；毒品；麻醉剂；给……下药
definition_en: a substance used to treat illness, an illegal substance taken for pleasure, a substance that alters the mind or body, or to give such a substance to someone
core_image: 一只贴着标签的小瓶，既可能救命，也可能夺走清醒
scene: 诊所的柜子里排着一排贴着标签的小瓶，瓶身反着冷光。 The doctor warned him not to mix the drug with alcohol.
sceneCN: 这里 drug 是「药物」（第 1 个义项：用于治疗疾病的药）；句意是医生告诫他不要把这药和酒混在一起。

collocations.zh: 给病人用药物使其麻木

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「药剂师；药商」
由本词与 store 复合，义为「药店；杂货药房」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「被下了药的；麻木的」

senses.title: A medicine
senses.definition: a substance used to treat, cure or prevent an illness or to relieve symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 用于治疗、治愈或预防疾病，或缓解症状的物质
senses.example: The drug lowered her blood pressure within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药在一小时内降低了她的血压。
senses.why: The word began in pharmacy, where a dried plant or prepared substance was the unit of treatment; this is still its neutral medical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起源于药学，那里一份干燥的草药或配好的制剂就是治疗的单位；这仍是它中性的医学义。

senses.title: An illegal substance
senses.definition: an illegal substance, often addictive, taken for pleasure or escape rather than for medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 常具成瘾性、非为治疗而只为快感或逃避而服用的非法物质
senses.example: The police seized a large amount of the drug at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在边境查获了大量这种毒品。
senses.why: When the same substances left the clinic and entered the street, the neutral word acquired a strong negative sense that now often comes first to mind.
senses.whyCN: 当同样的物质离开诊所、进入街头，这个中性词就带上了强烈的负面义，如今往往最先被想到。

senses.title: A substance affecting the mind or body
senses.titleCN: 麻醉剂；作用于身心的物质
senses.definition: a substance that alters consciousness, sensation or bodily function, such as a narcotic or anaesthetic
senses.definitionCN: 改变意识、感觉或身体机能的物质，如麻醉剂或镇静剂
senses.example: The patient was given a drug to ease the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给病人用了一种药来止痛。
senses.why: This sense sits between medicine and narcotic: the substance is used medically, but what it does is change how the body feels.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项介于药物与毒品之间：它被医学使用，但作用在于改变身体的感受。

senses.title: To give someone a drug
senses.definition: to give a drug to a person or animal, especially secretly or to make them unconscious
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或动物用药，尤指偷偷地或为使其失去知觉
senses.example: Someone had drugged his drink.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在他的饮料里下了药。
senses.why: The verb turns the substance into an act of control: one person quietly takes away another person's clear senses.
senses.whyCN: 动词把物质变成一种控制行为：一个人悄悄夺走另一个人清醒的意识。

intro.en: Drug entered English through Old French in the Middle Ages, and its further origin is genuinely uncertain; several explanations compete.
intro.cn: drug 在中世纪经由古法语进入英语，更早的来源确实不确定，存在几种相互竞争的解释。

items.en: Old French drogue meant a medicine or a substance used in pharmacy, and it is the immediate source of the English word.
items.cn: 古法语 drogue 意为「药物」或药房所用的「原料」，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: Middle English drogge appears in medical and trade texts, often for dried plant materials sold by apothecaries.
items.cn: 中古英语 drogge 出现在医学与贸易文本中，常指药剂师出售的干燥植物原料。

items.en: One common suggestion links the word to Dutch droog, dry, because many early drugs were dried herbs; this is plausible but not proved.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与荷兰语 droog（干燥）联系起来，因为早期药物多为干燥草药；此说合理但未获证明。

items.en: Other accounts point to an Arabic source through Mediterranean trade; the evidence is indirect and scholars do not agree.
items.cn: 另有说法认为它经地中海贸易来自阿拉伯语；证据是间接的，学界并无共识。

items.en: The word is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, at first in pharmacy; exact first uses are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪见于英语，最初用于药学；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense of an illegal or addictive substance developed in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, and the verb followed it.
items.cn: 「非法或成瘾性物质」这一义项在十九、二十世纪发展出来，动词用法也随之出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on drug or easily confused with it; the near-meaning group separates medicine, medication and remedy by their scope and tone.
note.cn: 形近组收由 drug 构成或容易混淆的词；近义组按范围与语气区分 medicine、medication 与 remedy。

entries.definition: A person who prepares and sells medicines; drug plus the person suffix -ist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指配制和出售药品的人，由 drug 加表人后缀 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: A shop that sells medicines and also household goods; drug plus store.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指出售药品并兼卖日用品的商店，由 drug 加 store 构成。

entries.definition: Having been given a drug, often secretly; the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指被下了药的，常指被人偷偷下药；由过去分词转作形容词。

entries.definition: A percussion instrument; it looks close to drug but has an unrelated musical origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鼓」；拼写与 drug 接近，但来源是另一条音乐词源。

entries.definition: A substance taken to treat illness; neutral and strongly medical, without the street sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「药、药物」，中性且医学色彩强，不含街头义。

entries.definition: A drug prescribed for a patient; formal and clinical, used mostly in medical contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「药物、处方药」，正式而临床，多用于医疗语境。

entries.definition: A treatment or cure, often a simple one; it stresses restoring health rather than the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疗法、补救办法」，常指简易疗法，强调恢复健康而非物质本身。

entries.definition: A drug that dulls pain and may cause sleep or addiction; a narrower, more technical term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「麻醉剂、毒品」，指镇痛并可能致睡或成瘾的药物，范围更窄、更技术化。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the pharmacy origin in view and then show how the same bottle acquired its darker sense.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子始终把药学来源放在眼前，再看同一只瓶子如何带上更阴暗的含义。

normal.en: Drug first meant a dried herb sold by an apothecary, so picture a paper packet of dried leaves.
normal.cn: drug 最初指药剂师出售的干燥草药，所以先想象一包干叶子。

normal.en: The verb is regular: drug, drugged, drugged, drugging; double the final g.
normal.cn: 这个动词是规则的：drug、drugged、drugged、drugging；词尾 g 要双写。

normal.en: Prescription drug is the medical side; drug abuse is the street side; the same word covers both.
normal.cn: prescription drug 是医学的一面，drug abuse 是街头的一面，同一个词覆盖两端。

normal.en: To drug someone is to take their clear senses away without asking.
normal.cn: to drug someone 就是在对方不知情时夺走其清醒的意识。

normal.en: Druggist and drugstore keep the old pharmacy meaning alive in everyday English.
normal.cn: druggist 与 drugstore 让古老的药学义在日常英语里继续活着。

abstract.en: Picture one small bottle on a shelf, with a label that could read either heal or harm.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上的一只小瓶，标签上既可能写着「治愈」，也可能写着「伤害」。

abstract.en: The same bottle moves from a clinic shelf to a street corner, and its meaning darkens with the journey.
abstract.cn: 同一只瓶子从诊所的架子走到街角，含义也随这段旅程变得阴暗。

abstract.en: Drug is a word about control: who decides what enters a body, and for what purpose.
abstract.cn: drug 是一个关于控制的词：由谁决定什么进入身体，又为了什么目的。

examples.en: The new drug has been approved for treating high blood pressure.
examples.cn: 这种新药已获准用于治疗高血压。

examples.en: The campaign warns young people against illegal drugs.
examples.cn: 这项运动警告年轻人远离非法毒品。

examples.en: The horse was drugged before the race and could not run.
examples.cn: 那匹马赛前被下了药，跑不起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: drug 本是药房里的一包干草药：治病时是药，滥用时是毒品，偷偷给人用就是「下药」。

root: 经由古法语 drogue（药物、药房原料）进入英语，更早来源不确定：一说与荷兰语 droog「干燥」有关，因早期药物多为干燥草药；另有经地中海贸易来自阿拉伯语的说法，均无定论。十四世纪起见于英语药学文本。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of drug follow one substance from the pharmacy shelf to the street: a medicine, an illegal habit, a mind-altering dose, and the act of giving it secretly.
sensesIntro.cn: drug 的四个义项让同一种物质从药房架子走到街头：药物、非法瘾品、改变身心的药剂，以及偷偷给人用药的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one labelled bottle that can either restore health or take away clear senses.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只贴标签的小瓶，既能恢复健康，也能夺走清醒。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: a prepared substance whose purpose is to treat or prevent illness.
branches.cn: 诊所线：以治疗或预防疾病为目的的制剂。

branches.en: THE STREET: the same substance sold illegally and taken for escape.
branches.cn: 街头线：同样的物质被非法出售，被用来逃避现实。

branches.en: THE BODY: a dose that changes consciousness, sensation or bodily function.
branches.cn: 身体线：改变意识、感觉或身体机能的剂量。

branches.en: THE ACT: giving the substance to someone, often without their knowledge.
branches.cn: 行为线：把这种物质给某人，往往在其不知情时。

branches.en: ONE SUBSTANCE, TWO REPUTATIONS: medicine and narcotic share a history and a word.
branches.cn: 同一物质，两种名声：药物与毒品共享一段历史和同一个词。

intro.en: Drug is a borrowed root with an uncertain deeper origin; English adds person, place and participle suffixes to build its family.
intro.cn: drug 是一个借入的词根，更深来源不确定；英语加表人、表地点和分词后缀来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is established; the Latin word for a drug, medicamentum, belongs to a different family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有确立的拉丁语祖先；拉丁语表示药物的 medicamentum 属于另一个词族。

items.example: The root serves as both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼作名词与动词。
它出现在 drug abuse 中。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「药剂师；药商」

definition_zh: 拖；拉；拖沓；沉闷乏味的事；阻力；拖着走
definition_en: to pull something heavy along the ground, or a dull boring experience
core_image: 一只箱子贴着地面被拖行，留下长长一道痕
scene: 搬家的下午，楼道里只剩一个人拖着箱子，轮子早坏了。 He had to drag the suitcase up three flights of stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 drag 是「拖、拉」（第 1 个义项）；句意是他不得不把行李箱拖上三层楼。

pos.zh: 名词：烦人的事；阻力；拖曳

derivatives.zh: 由 drag 加 -ing 构成，义为「拖拖拉拉的；令人疲惫的」
由 drag 加 -er 构成，义为「拖曳者；拖网船」
由 drag 加 net 复合而成，义为「拖网；大搜捕」

senses.title: To pull something heavy along
senses.definition: to pull something heavy along the ground or another surface
senses.definitionCN: 把沉重的东西在地面或别的表面上拉动
senses.example: They dragged the broken chair to the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把坏掉的椅子拖到院子里。
senses.why: The verb began as a strong pull through soil or mud, and that heavy scraping motion is still the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最初指在土壤或泥里用力拖，那种沉重的摩擦感至今仍是核心义。

senses.title: To move slowly and unwillingly
senses.definition: to move or go somewhere too slowly, often because you do not want to
senses.definitionCN: 移动得太慢，往往是因为不愿意去
senses.example: He dragged himself out of bed at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他中午才磨蹭着起床。
senses.why: When the body itself becomes the heavy object, the same pull turns into reluctant, slow movement.
senses.whyCN: 当身体自己成了那个沉重的物件，同样的「拉」就变成不情愿的缓慢移动。

senses.title: To continue for too long
senses.definition: to last longer than is wanted or interesting
senses.definitionCN: 持续时间超过人们的期待或兴趣
senses.example: The meeting dragged on for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会议拖了三个小时。
senses.why: Something that is dragged out is pulled longer than its natural length, so the phrase means prolonged.
senses.whyCN: 被拖出来的东西总比原本更长，所以这个词组表示「被拉长、拖久」。

senses.title: Something dull and tiring
senses.definition: an activity or event that is boring, slow, and unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 枯燥、缓慢又不愉快的活动或事件
senses.example: Waiting at the clinic was a real drag.
senses.exampleCN: 在诊所等候实在是一件苦差事。
senses.why: If an experience feels like a heavy load you must pull along, it becomes a drag in the slang sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果一段经历像是必须拖着走的沉重负担，它在口语里就变成了「苦差事」。

senses.title: Resistance in the air or water
senses.definition: the force that slows an object moving through air or water
senses.definitionCN: 物体在空气或水中移动时使其减速的力
senses.example: The plane's shape reduces drag at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种机型在高速时能减小阻力。
senses.why: Anything moving through a medium is held back as if something were pulling it backwards.
senses.whyCN: 任何在介质中前进的物体都被向后拽住，仿佛有什么东西在往后拖它。

intro.en: Drag is a Germanic verb of pulling, probably related to draw, and it has kept a heavy scraping feel.
intro.cn: drag 是表示「拉」的日耳曼语动词，可能与 draw 同源，一直带着沉重的摩擦感。

items.en: The root behind draw and drag is usually reconstructed as a pulling root; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: draw 与 drag 背后的词根一般被重构为一个表示「拉」的形式，确切形式仍有争议。

items.en: Dragan meant to draw or pull and became modern draw.
items.cn: 古英语 dragan 意为「拉、拖」，演变为现代的 draw。

items.en: A variant with a doubled g described pulling something heavy along the ground.
items.cn: 一个带双 g 的变体专门描述把重物贴着地面拖行。

items.en: The noun drag named a heavy sled or a hooked tool for fishing; dating of first use is approximate.
items.cn: 名词 drag 指沉重的雪橇或带钩的渔具；首次使用的年代只能大致推定。

items.en: The word extended to slow movement, boring events, air resistance and computer dragging.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到缓慢移动、乏味之事、空气阻力与计算机拖放操作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pulling root; the near-meaning group separates types of heavy pulling.
note.cn: 形近组共享「拉」的词根；近义组区分几种「费力拉」的方式。

entries.definition: To pull something toward you, or to sketch with lines.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拉；画」，与 drag 同源。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of drag.
entries.definitionCN: drag 的过去式与过去分词，注意末尾要双写 g 再加 -ed。

entries.definition: A net pulled along the bottom, or a widespread police search.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「拖网；大搜捕」，形象是「拖着网扫过」。

entries.definition: To move something toward you with force; it does not imply scraping.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拉」，不强调摩擦，是最中性的说法。

entries.definition: To pull something heavy over a long distance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「长途拖运」，强调距离与重量。

entries.definition: To pull sharply and repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用力猛拉」，是短促反复的拉。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the scraping sound and from the phrases that grew out of it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从摩擦声出发，并串联由它长出的短语。

normal.en: The doubled g and the hard final sound copy the noise of scraping.
normal.cn: 双写的 g 与结实的收音，模仿了拖擦时的声响。

normal.en: Drag on means the thing is pulled longer than it should be.
normal.cn: drag on 就是被拉得比本该有的更长。

normal.en: A drag of an evening is a load you had to pull through.
normal.cn: a drag of an evening 就是一整晚你必须拖过去的负担。

normal.en: Drag in physics is resistance, as if the air were pulling you back.
normal.cn: 物理里的 drag 是阻力，仿佛空气在把你往后拽。

normal.en: Drag and drop on a screen copies the hand motion exactly.
normal.cn: 屏幕上的 drag and drop 完全照搬了手上的拖拽动作。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase with a broken wheel leaving a line in the dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一只轮子坏掉的行李箱在灰尘里划出一道线。

abstract.en: Picture two people tugging a heavy sled uphill.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人拉着沉重的雪橇往坡上去。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands refuse to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，指针怎么都不肯动。

examples.en: She dragged the box across the floor.
examples.cn: 她把箱子拖过地板。

examples.en: The trial dragged on for months.
examples.cn: 这场审判拖了好几个月。

examples.en: Cleaning the whole flat was a drag.
examples.cn: 打扫整个公寓真是件苦差事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拽个」——拽着个重箱子在地上拖，drag 就是「拽着走」。

root: 日耳曼语动词，与古英语 dragan（拉、拖，今 draw）同源；中古英语出现带双 g 的变体 draggen，专指把重物贴地拖动。由「贴地拖行」引申为「磨蹭」、「拖久」，再引申为口语中的「苦差事」与物理上的「阻力」。

sensesIntro.en: The heavy scraping pull extends to reluctant motion, overlong events, dull chores and physical resistance.
sensesIntro.cn: 沉重的摩擦式拉动，延伸出不情愿的移动、过长的过程、乏味的差事与物理阻力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy box scraping along the ground, leaving a line.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重的箱子贴着地面摩擦前进，留下一道痕。

branches.en: PULLING: the basic sense is a heavy object moved along a surface.
branches.cn: 拉拽线：基本义是让重物贴着表面移动，即第一个义项。

branches.en: THE BODY: when the body is the weight, movement turns slow and unwilling.
branches.cn: 身体线：当身体成了那个重物，移动就变慢且不情愿，即第二个义项。

branches.en: TIME: an event pulled beyond its length becomes both a drag on and a drag.
branches.cn: 时间线：被拉得过长的事件，既说 drag on，也成了 a drag，即第三、四个义项。

branches.en: PHYSICS: moving through air or water is held back as if pulled backwards.
branches.cn: 物理线：在空气或水中前进被向后拽住，即第五个义项。

branches.en: A dragged object and aerodynamic drag both describe opposing force.
branches.cn: 被拖的物体与气动阻力，都在描述一种对抗的力量。

intro.en: Drag is a Germanic word that accepts English endings and compounds easily.
intro.cn: drag 是日耳曼语词，很容易接英语词尾与复合成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the root belongs to the Germanic family with draw.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语祖先；这个词根与 draw 同属日耳曼语族。

items.example: The old verb underlies both draw and drag.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老动词同时支撑 draw 与 drag。

items.example: It forms dragged after doubling the g.
items.exampleCN: 双写 g 之后它构成 dragged。

items.meaning: a thing or person that does

derivatives.zh: 由 drag 加 -ing 构成，义为「拖沓的；令人疲惫的」
由 drag 加 net 复合，义为「拖网；大搜捕」

definition_zh: 猛推；推挤；推
definition_en: to push someone or something roughly or forcefully
core_image: 一只手掌狠狠顶上去，把人逼得踉跄
scene: 人群里有人猛推了他一把。 Someone shoved him hard in the crowded hallway.
sceneCN: 这里 shove 是「猛推」（第 1 个义项：用力推开人或物）；句意：在拥挤的走廊里有人狠狠推了他一把。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词名词化，义为「推挤（行为）」
与 shove 同源的名词，义为「铲子；铲」

senses.title: To push roughly
senses.definition: to push someone or something roughly or forcefully
senses.definitionCN: 粗暴或用力地推开某人或某物
senses.example: The guard shoved the crowd back.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫把人群往后推。
senses.why: The core image is a hand driving force into someone, rougher than a gentle push.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是用手把力道砸进对方身上，比普通的推更粗暴，所以引出「猛推」义。

senses.title: To push something carelessly into a place
senses.definition: to put something somewhere quickly and carelessly
senses.definitionCN: 把某物随手快速塞到某个地方
senses.example: He shoved the papers into his bag.
senses.exampleCN: 他把文件胡乱塞进包里。
senses.why: Forcing things into a space is the same rough pushing motion applied to objects.
senses.whyCN: 把东西硬塞进空间，就是把「用力推」的动作用到物品上，义项由此延伸。

senses.title: To move oneself through a crowd
senses.definition: to push your way through a place or past people
senses.definitionCN: 用力推开人群往前挤
senses.example: She shoved past the reporters.
senses.exampleCN: 她从记者中间挤了过去。
senses.why: When the pusher and the mover are the same person, rough pushing becomes shoving through.
senses.whyCN: 当施力者与移动者是同一人，「猛推」就变成替自己开路的「挤」，义项随之成立。

senses.title: A rough push
senses.definition: a strong, rough push
senses.definitionCN: 一下用力而粗鲁的推
senses.example: He gave the door a hard shove.
senses.exampleCN: 他猛地推了一下那扇门。
senses.why: The action names the event itself, turning the motion into a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 动作本身被当作事件命名，推的行为变成了可数的名词，义项由动词转来。

intro.en: Shove is an old native English word for pushing with force.
intro.cn: shove 是英语本土的古老动词，本义就是用力推。

items.en: A reconstructed root *skeub- meant to push or shove.
items.cn: 重构词根 *skeub- 意为推、撞。

items.en: Scufan meant to push away or thrust.
items.cn: 古英语 scufan 意为推开、猛推。

items.en: The form evolved into shoven, keeping the pushing sense.
items.cn: 中古英语演变为 shoven，仍保留推的意义。

items.en: The careless sense of stuffing things into places appeared.
items.cn: 「胡乱塞进」的用法在这个时期出现。

items.en: The noun sense and the crowded-passage sense are both common today.
items.cn: 名词用法与「挤过去」的用法今天都很常用。

note.en: Shove is compared with its close relative shove- words and with other pushing verbs.
note.cn: 把 shove 与同族词以及其它表示推的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a tool with a broad blade for moving earth, or to move it with such a tool
entries.definitionCN: 铲子；用铲子铲，与 shove 同源于「推、掷」的动作

entries.definition: to walk by dragging the feet, or to mix cards
entries.definitionCN: 拖着脚走；洗牌，只是拼拼写近，词源与 shove 无关

entries.definition: to close something
entries.definitionCN: 关闭，拼写相近但来源不同

entries.definition: to press something to move it away from you
entries.definitionCN: 推，中性常用词，语气不如 shove 粗暴

entries.definition: to push suddenly and strongly
entries.definitionCN: 猛地一推、捅，强调突然发力

entries.definition: to push roughly against someone in a crowd
entries.definitionCN: 在人群中推挤、碰撞，强调拥挤场面

normalIntro.en: Shove pictures a hand driving into someone with force.
normalIntro.cn: shove 的画面是一只手带着力道顶上去。

normal.en: Someone shoved him hard in the hallway.
normal.cn: 走廊里有人狠狠推了他一把。

normal.en: He shoved the papers into his bag.
normal.cn: 他把文件胡乱塞进包里。

normal.en: She shoved past the reporters.
normal.cn: 她从记者中间挤了过去。

normal.en: He gave the door a hard shove.
normal.cn: 他猛地推了一下那扇门。

normal.en: Stop shoving in the queue.
normal.cn: 排队时别推来推去。

abstract.en: A shove is a push without politeness.
abstract.cn: shove 是不带礼貌的推。

abstract.en: Life sometimes shoves you off balance.
abstract.cn: 生活有时会把你猛推得站不稳。

abstract.en: One shove can start an argument.
abstract.cn: 一记猛推就能挑起争吵。

examples.en: Someone shoved him hard in the crowded hallway.
examples.cn: 在拥挤的走廊里有人狠狠推了他一把。

examples.en: He shoved the papers into his bag and left.
examples.cn: 他把文件胡乱塞进包里就走了。

examples.en: The guard shoved the crowd back from the gate.
examples.cn: 警卫把人群从大门口往后推。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沙夫」——想象一只手掌拍在背上「沙」的一声，人就「伏」了下去，这就是被人猛推一把的 shove。

root: 源自古英语 scufan（推开、猛推），一般可追溯到日耳曼语词根 *skeub-（推、撞），与 shovel（铲子）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shove means to push roughly, to stuff things carelessly, to push through, or the push itself as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: shove 既指粗暴地推，也指胡乱塞放、挤过去，还可作名词指猛推的动作。

core.en: A hand driving force into someone or something.
core.cn: 一只手把力道砸进人或物身上。

branches.en: The guard drives the crowd back with rough force.
branches.cn: 警卫用粗暴的力道把人群顶回去。

branches.en: The pushing motion becomes stuffing things carelessly.
branches.cn: 推的动作变成胡乱塞放东西。

branches.en: The pusher pushes himself through the crowd.
branches.cn: 施力者用推给自己在人群里开路。

branches.en: The action names the rough push itself.
branches.cn: 动作反过来命名那次猛推。

branches.en: All senses share one rough, careless force.
branches.cn: 各义项共享同一股粗暴随意的力。

intro.en: Shove is a short native verb whose family comes from an old pushing root.
intro.cn: shove 是简短的本土动词，其词族源自古老的「推」词根。

latinIntro.en: Shove is Germanic, not Latin, so no Latin relatives exist; the Germanic family is listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: shove 属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，没有拉丁同族词，此处列出日耳曼语词族。

items.exampleCN: 有人从背后猛推了他一下。

items.structure: Old English scofl, from the same pushing root
items.meaning: a tool for pushing and lifting earth
items.example: He shoveled snow off the path.
There was a lot of shoving at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 大门口发生了不少推挤。

items.meaning: to leave; to push a boat away from shore
items.example: It is late; we should shove off.

items.meaning: to treat someone roughly or bossily
items.example: I will not be shoved around.

items.meaning: to press something to move it away
items.example: Push the door, do not pull.
He thrust the letter into his pocket.

items.meaning: to drag the feet or mix cards

derivatives.zh: 同源词，铲子；铲
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「推挤行为」

definition_zh: 家伙；哥们；老兄；花花公子；西部度假游客
definition_en: an informal word for a man, especially a friend, or a fashionable city man visiting the countryside
core_image: 拍肩打招呼：一句随口喊出的哥们称呼
scene: 海滩边两个年轻人冲浪归来，互相击掌，其中一人笑着朝另一人喊了一声。 Hey dude, that wave was huge!
sceneCN: 这里 dude 是「哥们、老兄」（第 2 个义项：对男性朋友的随口称呼）；句意是“嘿哥们，刚才那个浪真大！”，体现这个词的口语寒暄用法。

pos.zh: 家伙；哥们；老兄；花花公子；城里来的度假游客
打扮；盛装打扮（常用于短语 dude up）

collocations.zh: （供城市游客体验的）牛仔度假牧场
某个家伙；某个不知名的人

derivatives.zh: 由 dude（城里游客）+ ranch（牧场）构成的复合名词，指专供城市人体验牛仔生活的度假牧场
由 dude 加女性后缀 -ette 构成的戏谑说法，指女版哥们
由 dude 加 -ism 后缀构成的戏谑词，指一种源自电影的悠闲生活哲学

senses.title: A man; a guy
senses.definition: an informal word for any man or young male person
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对任意男性或年轻男子的称呼
senses.example: Some dude asked me for directions at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 车站有个家伙向我问路。
senses.why: The word was first used for a particular kind of man, then widened to mean almost any man in casual talk.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初只指某一类讲究的男性，后来在口语中泛化，几乎可以指任何一个男人，词义由窄变宽。

senses.title: A friendly way to address someone
senses.definition: a friendly informal way to address a friend, especially among young people
senses.definitionCN: 对朋友friendly的随口称呼，年轻人之间尤其常用
senses.example: Dude, you will not believe what happened today.
senses.exampleCN: 老兄，你绝对想不到今天发生了什么。
senses.why: Calling someone by a relaxed noun turns the word into pure address, showing closeness rather than description.
senses.whyCN: 当称呼不再描述对方而是纯粹拉近距离时，名词就变成了寒暄语，体现亲近感而非字面身份。

senses.title: A fashionable city man
senses.titleCN: 城里时髦男子；花花公子
senses.definition: a man from the city who dresses very carefully and pays too much attention to style
senses.definitionCN: 衣着讲究、过分注重外表的城里男子
senses.example: The original dude wore fancy clothes and knew nothing about farm work.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的花花公子穿着华丽，却对农活一窍不通。
senses.why: The earliest recorded sense, from late nineteenth century American English, focused on showy clothing and city manners.
senses.whyCN: 这是十九世纪末美式英语里最早记录的义项，核心在于显眼的穿着与都市做派，是后来一切引申的源头。

senses.title: A city visitor at a ranch
senses.definition: a city person vacationing on a western ranch, inexperienced in ranch life
senses.definitionCN: 到西部牧场度假、缺乏牧场生活经验的城市人
senses.example: The ranch hands laughed at the dude trying to saddle a horse.
senses.exampleCN: 牧场工人笑话那个连马鞍都不会装的城市游客。
senses.why: Because such visitors were well dressed and unskilled, the fashionable sense was applied to them as a mild joke.
senses.whyCN: 这类游客衣着体面却笨手笨脚，于是时髦男子的称呼被挪用到他们身上，带着温和的调侃。

senses.title: A showily dressed, unskilled outsider
senses.definition: a person whose fine appearance contrasts with their lack of practical experience
senses.definitionCN: 外表光鲜但缺乏实际本领的人
senses.example: To the cowboys, every dude looked the same: neat suit, useless hands.
senses.exampleCN: 在牛仔眼里，所有讲究人看起来都一样：西装笔挺，两手笨拙。
senses.why: The contrast between polished surface and clumsy action became the very definition of the type.
senses.whyCN: 光鲜外表与笨拙行动之间的反差，本身就成了这一类人的定义，词义聚焦在「虚有其表」。

senses.title: An unnamed person
senses.definition: used for a person whose name is unknown or not worth mentioning
senses.definitionCN: 指姓名不详或不必点名的某个人
senses.example: A dude in a red jacket left this package here.
senses.exampleCN: 一个穿红夹克的家伙把包裹落在这儿了。
senses.why: Casual nouns often become placeholders when a speaker does not know or care about identity.
senses.whyCN: 当说话人不了解或不在意对方身份时，随意名词自然变成指代工具，词义从身份滑向「某人」。

senses.title: An ordinary, relaxed man
senses.definition: a man seen as easygoing and unpretentious, often in phrases like just a regular dude
senses.definitionCN: 随和不做作的男人，常见于 just a regular dude 之类的说法
senses.example: He is a famous actor, but he is really just a regular dude.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个名演员，但其实就是个随和的普通人。
senses.why: As the teasing edge faded, the word kept its relaxed flavor and began to mean down-to-earth rather than showy.
senses.whyCN: 调侃意味淡去后，词保留了轻松随意的语感，语义从「炫耀外表」翻转为「接地气」，是词义的反向漂移。

senses.title: To dress up smartly
senses.definition: to dress oneself in fancy clothes, usually in the phrase dude up
senses.definitionCN: 穿上讲究的衣服，通常用于短语 dude up
senses.example: They all duded up for the awards dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为颁奖晚宴都盛装打扮了一番。
senses.why: The noun for a finely dressed man was turned into a verb describing the act of becoming finely dressed.
senses.whyCN: 指人的名词被活用作动词，描述「变成那种人」的动作，即通过装扮成为讲究穿着的男子。

intro.en: Dude is a young American slang word whose ultimate origin is uncertain; it grew from the idea of a fastidiously dressed man and gradually became a general friendly address.
intro.cn: dude 是年轻的美国俚语词，其最终来源不确定；它从「讲究穿着的男子」这一核心义出发，逐渐演变成通用的友好称呼。

items.en: The word is first recorded in American English around 1883, meaning a man who dresses fastidiously; its ultimate origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 该词约在 1883 年首次见于美国英语，指衣着过分讲究的男子；其最终来源不确定。

items.en: One common hypothesis links it to duds, an older slang word for clothes, but this connection is generally believed rather than proved.
items.cn: 一种常见假说把它与 duds（旧时指衣服的俚语）联系起来，但这只是一般认为，并未确证。

items.en: Some scholars suggest influence from dandy, the word for a fashionable man, or from the nonsense name Yankee Doodle; these are competing hypotheses and should not be forced into one choice.
items.cn: 也有学者提出它可能受了 dandy（时髦男子）或滑稽歌名 Yankee Doodle 的影响；这些是并列假说，不宜强行择定。

items.en: In the early twentieth century the word spread to dude ranch, a resort ranch for city visitors, fixing the sense of the inexperienced city tourist.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，该词扩展出 dude ranch 一语，指接待城市游客的度假牧场，坐实了「城市游客」这一义项。

items.en: From surf and youth culture in California, dude became a relaxed address for friends of any background, shedding its mocking tone.
items.cn: 经加州冲浪与青年文化推广，dude 变成了不分背景的朋友间随意称呼，褪去了嘲讽色彩。

items.en: Today dude is one of the most common informal address words in American English, and the verb phrase dude up keeps the old sense of dressing smartly.
items.cn: 如今 dude 是美式英语最常见的随意称呼之一，动词短语 dude up 则保留着旧的「盛装打扮」之义。

note.en: Dude is surrounded by short slang words for men and clothes; several look alike, others share the same social flavor.
note.cn: dude 周围聚集了一批指男性与衣着的短小俚语词：有的拼写相近，有的社会语感相似。

entries.definition: something that fails to work or impress
entries.definitionCN: 失败品；无用的东西——只比 dude 少一个字母，词源关系一般认为与衣着义相关但存疑，二者用法完全不同

entries.definition: informal word for clothes
entries.definitionCN: 衣服（俚语）——被认为是 dude 的可能来源之一，但联系未确证

entries.definition: a man who cares greatly about elegant dress
entries.definitionCN: 讲究穿戴的花花公子——语义与 dude 的旧义几乎重叠，有学者认为它影响了 dude 的形成

entries.definition: the most general informal word for a man
entries.definitionCN: 家伙、男人——最通用的口语说法，比 dude 更中性，不带拉近距离的寒暄色彩

entries.definition: a friend, used warmly in address
entries.definitionCN: 伙计、好友——与 dude 的称呼用法接近，但更强调友谊本身

entries.definition: a friend or companion, common British address
entries.definitionCN: 伙伴、老兄——英式口语中与 dude 功能对应的称呼词

normalIntro.en: Use the word family and real phrases to lock dude in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 用词族与真实短语把 dude 牢牢锁进记忆。

normal.en: duds means clothes; dude may have grown from dressing in fine duds.
normal.cn: duds 意为衣服；dude 一般认为可能与「穿讲究的衣服」相关。

normal.en: dude ranch is a resort where city dudes learn cowboy life.
normal.cn: dude ranch 是城市「讲究人」体验牛仔生活的度假牧场。

normal.en: dude up = dress up; the noun became a verb for dressing smartly.
normal.cn: dude up = 盛装打扮；名词活用作动词表示精心装扮。

normal.en: dandy is the elegant cousin; both began as words for fashionable men.
normal.cn: dandy 是它优雅的表亲：两词都从「时髦男子」起家。

normal.en: Hey dude! Repeat the greeting until it feels natural.
normal.cn: 反复念 Hey dude!，直到招呼语变得脱口而出。

abstract.en: Picture a city man in a shiny suit standing awkwardly in a cowboy field.
abstract.cn: 想象一个穿亮西装的城里人尴尬地站在牛仔牧场上。

abstract.en: Hear two surfers slap palms and shout dude after a big wave.
abstract.cn: 耳边回响两个冲浪者击掌大喊 dude 的声音。

abstract.en: Feel the tap on the shoulder: a casual word that turns strangers into pals.
abstract.cn: 感受拍肩的力道：一个把陌生人变成哥们儿的随意称呼。

examples.en: Dude, you left your phone on the table.
examples.cn: 老兄，你把手机落在桌上了。

examples.en: In the 1880s a dude meant a man who dressed far too elegantly.
examples.cn: 在十九世纪八十年代，dude 指穿得过分讲究的男子。

examples.en: The dude ranch was full of city visitors wearing brand-new boots.
examples.cn: 牛仔度假牧场里挤满了穿着崭新靴子的城市游客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斗的」——见面喊一声 dude（斗的），像凑过来拍肩逗弄一下哥们，不是真在打斗。

root: 词源存疑：dude 为十九世纪末美国俚语，一般认为可能与 duds（衣服）相关，另有受 dandy 或 Yankee Doodle 影响的假说，均未确证；无可追溯的拉丁或希腊词根。

sensesIntro.en: From the oldest sense of a fastidiously dressed city man, dude widened to ranch visitors, then to any man, and finally into a friendly address and a verb for dressing up.
sensesIntro.cn: dude 从「讲究穿着的城里男子」这一最早义项出发，先扩展到牧场游客，再泛化为任意男人，最终变成友好称呼与「盛装打扮」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a polished city man stepping into a rough, casual world
core.cn: 核心意象：一个衣着光鲜的城里人，走进粗犷随意的世界

branches.en: The oldest pole: showy clothes and city manners.
branches.cn: 最古老的一极：显眼的穿着与都市做派。

branches.en: The word travels west with city tourists on vacation ranches.
branches.cn: 词随城市游客一路向西，落在度假牧场上。

branches.en: Generalizing from type to any unnamed man.

senses.title: The system of production and trade
senses.titleCN: 经济体系：一国生产与贸易的系统
senses.definition: the system by which a country or region produces, distributes and consumes goods, services and money
senses.definitionCN: 国家或地区生产、分配与消费商品、服务和货币的系统
senses.example: The economy slowed after the harvest failed.
senses.exampleCN: 收成失败后经济放缓。
senses.why: The Greek word first meant household management; as states took on the same task, the word grew to name a whole national system.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词起初表示家务管理；当国家承担同样的任务，这个词就扩大为指整个国家系统。

senses.title: Careful use of resources
senses.definition: the careful avoidance of waste in money, fuel, time or materials
senses.definitionCN: 在金钱、燃料、时间或材料上谨慎避免浪费
senses.example: The office introduced an economy of paper and ink.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室推行了纸张与墨水的节约措施。
senses.why: The older household sense survives here: a good manager wastes little, and that habit is itself called economy.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的家户义在这里留存：好当家人很少浪费，而这种习惯本身就叫 economy。

senses.title: A saving made
senses.definition: a specific saving or reduction in spending, often plural as economies
senses.definitionCN: 具体的一笔节省或开支削减，常用复数 economies
senses.example: The new heating system brought real economies in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 新的供暖系统在冬天带来了实实在在的节省。
senses.why: A habit of thrift produces concrete results, and each result is an economy rather than the habit itself.
senses.whyCN: 节俭的习惯会产生具体结果，每一个结果都是一项 economy，而不是习惯本身。

senses.title: The cheapest travel class
senses.titleCN: 经济舱：最便宜的出行等级
senses.definition: the cheapest class of seating on an aircraft or train, or the lowest grade of service
senses.definitionCN: 飞机或火车上最便宜的座位等级，或最低档次的服务
senses.example: She flew economy and spent the saving on a better hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐经济舱，把省下的钱花在更好的酒店上。
senses.why: Airlines borrowed the thrift sense: economy class is the class chosen to spend little.
senses.whyCN: 航空公司借用了「节俭」义：经济舱就是为少花钱而选的舱位。

intro.en: Economy is older in English than economics, and it reached the meaning of a national system only in the modern period.
intro.cn: economy 在英语中出现得比 economics 早，而「国家经济体系」义要到近现代才形成。

items.en: The compound meant household management, with oikos 'house' and nomos 'rule'.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为家务管理，由 oikos「房子」与 nomos「规则」构成。

items.en: Latin kept the sense of management, including the management of public revenue.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留「管理」义，也包括公共收入的管理。

items.en: Economy entered English as the management of a household or establishment.
items.cn: economy 进入英语时指家户或机构的管理。

items.en: The word was applied to the resources of a state, and the national sense became dominant.
items.cn: 这个词被用到国家的资源上，「国民经济」义逐渐占据主导。

items.en: Thrift, savings and travel class followed as narrower everyday uses of the same idea.
items.cn: 节俭、节省与舱位等级随后作为同一想法的日常窄义出现。

note.en: The look-alike group separates economy from the study, the adjectives and the person; the near-meaning group gathers words for thrift.
note.cn: 形近组把 economy 与学科、形容词及指人词分开；近义组收表示节俭的词。

entries.definition: The academic study of the economy, not the economy itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对经济的研究学科，而不是经济本身。

entries.definition: An adjective relating to the economy or to economics.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，与 economy 或 economics 相关。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning thrifty or cheap to run.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「节约的、使用成本低的」。

entries.definition: Careful management of money, avoiding waste.
entries.definitionCN: 对金钱的谨慎管理，避免浪费。

entries.definition: A reduction in cost, or money set aside.
entries.definitionCN: 成本上的削减，或存起来的钱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a national network, to a habit of thrift, to one concrete saving, to a seat on a plane.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从全国网络，走到节俭习惯、一笔具体节省，再到飞机上的一个座位。

normal.en: Economy is the thing itself; economics is the study of the thing.
normal.cn: economy 是事物本身，economics 是对这事物的研究。

normal.en: A household that wastes nothing is the small model of a national economy.
normal.cn: 一个不浪费的家户，就是国民经济的小模型。

normal.en: One saving is an economy; many savings are economies.
normal.cn: 一笔节省是一项 economy；许多笔就是 economies。

normal.en: Chemists speak of economy of effort, drivers of fuel economy: thrift applied to a resource.
normal.cn: 化学家说 economy of effort，司机说 fuel economy：都是把节俭用到某种资源上。

normal.en: A false economy costs more later than it saves now.
normal.cn: a false economy 现在省下的，日后要花更多。

abstract.en: The same threads can be pulled tight by thrift, or cut into a ticket class.
abstract.cn: 同一张网可以被节俭拉紧，也可以被切出一个舱位等级。

abstract.en: Economy means a managed whole, whether a country, a budget or a seat.
abstract.cn: economy 意味着一个被管理的整体，无论国家、预算还是一个座位。

scene: 会议开到深夜，几个人围着地图争论，最后有人把笔往桌上一放。 They determined the route before sunrise.

senses.title: Decide firmly

senses.example: They determined the route before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在日出前定下了路线。
senses.why: A choice becomes real only when it is written down.
senses.whyCN: 选择只有被写下来，才算真正落地。

senses.title: Find out exactly
senses.definition: to discover a fact or an amount by careful study
senses.definitionCN: 通过仔细研究弄清一个事实或数量
senses.example: Tests will determine the cause of the fault.
senses.exampleCN: 测试将查明故障的原因。
senses.why: The answer is already there; you only fix its outline.

senses.title: Control the result

intro.en: Determine comes from Latin determinare, to set a boundary, formed from de- and terminus, a boundary stone, and it came through French.

items.en: French determiner kept both the legal and the everyday sense.

items.en: English used it for deciding a question and for fixing a date.

examples.cn: 她下定决心要跑完这场比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 determine 记成「地特敏」：de 是定下，termin 是边界，把边界一钉，事情就定下来、也查清楚了。

root: 来自拉丁语 determinare，由 de-（加强）与 terminus（界石、边界）组成，经古法语 determiner 进入英语。本义是划定界限，引申为把问题定下来、作出决定，再引申为查明与支配。

sensesIntro.en: From drawing a line through a choice, to fixing the outline of a fact, to being the fact that rules the rest.
sensesIntro.cn: 从在众多选择中划下一道线，到钉住一个事实的轮廓，再到成为支配其余一切的那个事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen pressing a firm line across a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支笔在地图上压出一道坚定的线。

branches.en: The first sense is the stroke that turns thinking into a choice.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把思考变成选择的那一笔。

branches.en: The second sense is the same stroke drawn around a hidden fact.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是围着隐藏事实画下的同一笔。

branches.en: The third sense is a line so strong that other things must follow it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一条强到别的都得顺着它走的线。

branches.en: Deciding and discovering both end with a boundary that holds.
branches.cn: 作决定与查真相，最后都落到一条立得住的边界上。

branches.en: What you find out often becomes what controls the outcome.
branches.cn: 你查明的东西，常常就成了支配结果的东西。

intro.en: Determine stands at the centre of a family about limits, decisions and exact findings.
intro.cn: determine 站在一族词的中心，这族词关于界限、决定与精确查明。

latinIntro.en: The base is terminus, a boundary stone, and de- gives the act of fixing it.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 terminus（界石），前缀 de- 给出「把它钉住」这个动作。

items.meaning: to decide or find out exactly
items.example: We must determine the facts first.

items.meaning: a word that limits a noun
items.example: The word this is a determiner.
The plant is of indeterminate height.

items.meaning: the act of settling a matter
items.example: Determining the winner took an hour.

definition_zh: 专家；专科医生；专营店
definition_en: a person with deep knowledge of one field, a doctor in one branch of medicine, or a shop dealing in one kind of goods
core_image: 一位医生摘下眼镜，指着心脏影像图向年轻同事讲解
scene: 她是心脏病方面的专家。 She is a specialist in heart disease.
sceneCN: 这里 specialist 是「专家」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她是心脏病方面的专家。

derivatives.zh: 专攻；专门从事
专业化；专门化

senses.title: An expert
senses.definition: a person who knows a great deal about one subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某一学科了解极多的人
senses.example: She is a specialist in heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 她是心脏病方面的专家。
senses.why: This is the general sense of a person narrowed to one field.
senses.whyCN: 这是把一个人限定在一个领域的通用含义。

senses.title: A medical expert
senses.definition: a doctor trained in one branch of medicine
senses.definitionCN: 受过某一医学分支训练的医生
senses.example: He was referred to a heart specialist.
senses.exampleCN: 他被转诊给一位心脏专科医生。
senses.why: Medicine adopted the word for doctors who limit their practice.
senses.whyCN: 医学界用这个词指限定执业范围的医生。

senses.title: A one-field shop
senses.definition: a shop or firm that deals in one kind of goods
senses.definitionCN: 只经营某一类商品的商店或公司
senses.example: The shop is a specialist in rare books.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店专营珍本书籍。
senses.why: A business can be a specialist by narrowing what it sells.
senses.whyCN: 商家通过缩小经营范围，也能成为某一领域的专门店。

intro.en: Specialist is special with the suffix for a person devoted to a field.
intro.cn: specialist 是 special 加上表示「专注于某领域的人」的后缀。

items.en: Specialis meant of a particular kind.
items.cn: specialis 意为属于某一特定种类的。

items.en: Spécialiste named one devoted to a single study.
items.cn: spécialiste 指专注于单一学问的人。

items.en: Specialist entered English in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: specialist 于十九世纪进入英语。

items.en: Medicine used it for doctors of one branch.
items.cn: 医学用它指某一分支的医生。

items.en: Shops and firms adopted it for narrow trade.
items.cn: 商店和公司用它表示专营某一类业务。

note.en: Specialist is compared with look-alike words and words for experts.
note.cn: 把 specialist 与形近词以及表示专家的词作比较。

entries.definition: to focus on one field

normalIntro.en: A specialist is a person who has chosen one field and gone deep.
normalIntro.cn: specialist 是选定一个领域并深入下去的人。

normal.en: She is a specialist in heart disease.
normal.cn: 她是心脏病方面的专家。

normal.en: He was referred to a heart specialist.
normal.cn: 他被转诊给一位心脏专科医生。

normal.en: The shop is a specialist in rare books.
normal.cn: 这家店专营珍本书籍。

normal.en: The team hired a computer specialist.
normal.cn: 团队聘请了一位计算机专家。

normal.en: Specialist training takes many years.
normal.cn: 专业培训需要很多年。

abstract.en: To specialize is to trade width for depth.
abstract.cn: 专精，是用广度换深度。

abstract.en: Every specialist was once a curious beginner.
abstract.cn: 每位专家都曾是好奇的初学者。

abstract.en: The narrower the field, the deeper the well.
abstract.cn: 领域越窄，井就越深。

examples.cn: 她是心脏病方面的专家。

examples.en: The shop is a specialist in rare books.

dict_mnemonic.text: specialist 由 special 加 -ist 构成，指「专注于某一领域的人」，即专家、专科医生；动词 specialize 是「专攻」，名词 specialization 是「专业化」，specialist in 是「……方面的专家」。

root: 由拉丁语 specialis（特定种类的）加希腊来源的后缀 -ist（从事者）构成，指专注于某一领域的人，后特指专科医生。

sensesIntro.en: Specialist means an expert in one field, a doctor of one branch, or a shop dealing in one kind of goods.
sensesIntro.cn: specialist 指某一领域的专家、某一医学分支的专科医生，或专营某类商品的商店。

core.en: A person or business narrowed to one field.
core.cn: 收窄到一个领域的人或机构。

branches.en: One mind holds a single subject in depth.
branches.cn: 一个人深入掌握一门学问。

branches.en: A doctor studies only the heart.
branches.cn: 一位医生只研究心脏。

branches.en: A small shop sells only rare books.
branches.cn: 一家小店只卖珍本书。

branches.en: The expert and the doctor both earn trust through depth.
branches.cn: 专家与医生都凭深度赢得信任。

branches.en: A narrow practice can belong to a person or a shop.
branches.cn: 专精的领域可以属于一个人，也可以属于一家店。

intro.en: Specialist connects to verbs and nouns of narrowing focus.
intro.cn: specialist 与表示聚焦的动词和名词相连。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is specialis, of a particular kind, from species, a kind.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 specialis（特定种类的），源于 species（种类）。

items.example: Fish soup is the house specialty.

definition_zh: 天花板；顶棚；上限；云底高度
definition_en: the inner surface at the top of a room, or the highest level that something is allowed to reach
core_image: 头顶上那层封住房间的平面
scene: 老房子的房间很高。 A single lamp hung from the high ceiling.
sceneCN: 这里 ceiling 指「天花板」（第 1 个义项：房间顶部的内表面）；句意是一盏灯从高高的天花板上垂下来。

derivatives.zh: 给…装天花板
有…天花板的

senses.title: The top surface of a room
senses.definition: the inside surface that covers the top of a room
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖房间顶部的内表面
senses.example: The ceiling is painted white.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板刷成了白色。
senses.why: The old verb meant to line or panel a room, and the panel above your head became the ceiling.
senses.whyCN: 旧动词意为给房间装衬板，头顶上那层衬板就成了天花板。

senses.title: The highest allowed level
senses.definition: the greatest amount or level that is officially allowed or possible
senses.definitionCN: 官方允许或可能达到的最大数量或水平
senses.example: The government set a ceiling on rents.
senses.exampleCN: 政府给租金设了上限。
senses.why: A ceiling is a fixed surface you cannot rise above, so any hard limit borrows the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 天花板是一层无法越过的固定平面，于是任何硬性限制都借用了这个画面。

senses.title: The height of the cloud base
senses.definition: the height above the ground at which the lowest clouds begin, used in flying
senses.definitionCN: 最低云层离地面的高度，用于飞行
senses.example: The pilot reported a low ceiling over the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员报告海岸上空云底很低。
senses.why: To a pilot the cloud base is literally a roof over the aircraft, so the room word fits.
senses.whyCN: 对飞行员来说，云底字面上就是飞机头顶的屋顶，房间用词正好合用。

intro.en: Ceiling comes from an old verb meaning to line or hide, not from any word for sky.
intro.cn: ceiling 来自一个意为衬里或遮盖的旧动词，与表示天空的词无关。

items.en: Celare meant to hide or conceal, and its French descendant kept that sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celare 意为隐藏或遮盖，其法语后裔保留了这个意思。

items.en: Celer meant to conceal, and also to panel or line the inside of a room.
items.cn: 古法语 celer 意为遮盖，也指给房间内侧装衬板。

items.en: Celen names the panelling of walls and roofs, especially the upper lining of a room.
items.cn: 中古英语 celen 指给墙和屋顶装衬板，尤其是房间上部的衬层。

items.en: Ceiling settles as the noun for the inner roof of a room.
items.cn: 十六世纪 ceiling 固定为指房间内侧顶面的名词。

items.en: The word spreads to price ceilings, glass ceilings and the cloud base seen by pilots.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词扩展到价格上限、无形障碍以及飞行员所见的云底。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the old verb and its adjective, while the meaning group gives other upper limits.
note.cn: 形近组保留旧动词及其形容词，近义组给出其他上部或限度说法。

entries.definition: to fit a room with a ceiling
entries.definitionCN: 给房间装天花板

entries.definition: having a ceiling of a stated kind
entries.definitionCN: 有某种天花板的

entries.definition: the outer covering on top of a building
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物顶部的外层覆盖

entries.definition: an upper limit placed on an amount
entries.definitionCN: 对数量设定的上限

entries.definition: the greatest amount allowed
entries.definitionCN: 允许的最大数量

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the conceal root, the price phrases and the false link with sky.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用遮盖词根、价格搭配，以及与天空的错误联想。

normal.en: Ceiling and conceal share the Latin root celare, to hide, because a ceiling covers the room.
normal.cn: ceiling 与 conceal 共享拉丁语词根 celare（隐藏），因为天花板正是把房间盖住。

normal.en: The word has nothing to do with the Latin for sky, however tempting that link feels.
normal.cn: 尽管这层联想很诱人，这个词与拉丁语中表示天空的词毫无关系。

normal.en: Price ceiling and glass ceiling keep the limit sense in economics and at work.
normal.cn: price ceiling 与 glass ceiling 把上限义留在经济学与职场里。

normal.en: Hit the ceiling means explode with anger, as if your head struck the roof.
normal.cn: hit the ceiling 意思是暴怒，仿佛头撞到了屋顶。

normal.en: The plural ceilings simply adds an s to the -ing noun.
normal.cn: 复数 ceilings 只在 -ing 名词后加 s。

abstract.en: Picture a bare bulb swinging above a white plaster surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一只光灯泡在白色灰泥顶面下摆动。

abstract.en: Picture a pilot looking up at a flat grey layer of cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象飞行员抬头望见平坦的灰色云层。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing down on a rising graph line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把上升的曲线按住。

examples.en: The ceiling is too low for a tall bookshelf.
examples.cn: 天花板太低，放不下高书架。

examples.en: They put a ceiling on ticket prices.
examples.cn: 他们给票价设了上限。

examples.en: She has broken the glass ceiling in her company.
examples.cn: 她打破了公司里的无形晋升障碍。

dict_mnemonic.text: ceiling 可以想成「see 到顶」：抬头看见的那一层平面，就是天花板，也是上限。

root: 源自古法语 celer（遮盖、装衬板），上溯拉丁语 celare（隐藏），与表示天空的词无关。

sensesIntro.en: A lining that hides the roof beams becomes the room's upper surface, then any level you cannot rise above.
sensesIntro.cn: 遮住屋顶梁的衬层变成房间上部表面，再变成任何无法越过的水平线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat layer sealed over the space above your head.
core.cn: 核心意象：在头顶空间上封住的一层平面。

branches.en: The room surface keeps the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 房间顶面保留了最古老、最具体的义项。

branches.en: A limit borrows the picture of a surface you cannot pass.
branches.cn: 上限借用了无法穿过的平面这一画面。

branches.en: The cloud base becomes a roof for aircraft.
branches.cn: 云底成了飞机头顶的屋顶。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of a top that stops upward movement.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「顶端阻止上升」的意思。

branches.en: Both are technical extensions of one plain physical image.
branches.cn: 两者都是同一个具体画面在技术领域的延伸。

intro.en: Ceiling keeps the old verb ceil and a participle-like adjective, plus compounds.
intro.cn: ceiling 保留了旧动词 ceil 和类似分词的形容词，并有若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb celare, to hide, underlies the word through French celer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 celare（隐藏）经法语 celer 构成这个词的底层来源。
