definition_zh: 眼泪；泪水；泪珠；撕开；扯破；撕裂；拉伤；破洞；飞奔
definition_en: a drop of salty liquid from the eye; or to pull paper, cloth, or something apart quickly and with force
core_image: 眼角涌出的水珠，和双手把一张纸撕成两半
scene: 她读完信的最后一行，泪水模糊了纸上的字迹。 She brushed away a tear as she folded the old letter.
sceneCN: 这里 tear 是「眼泪、泪珠」（第 1 个义项：从眼睛流出的咸水滴）；句意：她折起旧信时拭去一滴泪。

derivatives.zh: 由名词 tear 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「含泪的；泪流满面的」
由名词 tear 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「眼泪汪汪的」
由 tear 与 drop 合成的复合词，义为「泪珠；泪滴状物」
由名词 tear 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「没有眼泪的」

senses.title: A drop of salty liquid from the eye
senses.definition: a drop of salty liquid that flows from the eye, usually because of strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 从眼睛流出的一滴咸味液体，通常由强烈情绪引起
senses.example: A single tear rolled down her cheek during the farewell scene.
senses.exampleCN: 告别那一幕里，一滴泪从她的脸颊滑落。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is pure image: water rising from the eye when feeling overflows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的层面就是画面本身：情绪满溢时，水从眼角涌出来。

senses.title: To pull paper or cloth apart with force
senses.definition: to pull paper, cloth, or similar material apart quickly and with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力快速地把纸、布等材料分开或弄破
senses.example: He tore the letter into pieces and threw them away.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信撕成碎片扔掉了。
senses.why: The verb comes from a different ancient root meaning to split or flay, so the core is force separating one thing into parts.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自另一个古老词根，本义是劈开、剥开，核心是用力把一个整体分开。

senses.title: To injure a muscle or ligament by stretching it too far
senses.definition: to injure a muscle or ligament by stretching or pulling it too violently
senses.definitionCN: 因过度拉扯而使肌肉或韧带受伤
senses.example: The sprinter tore a muscle in his right leg during the race.
senses.exampleCN: 短跑运动员比赛中右腿肌肉拉伤了。
senses.why: Body tissue is imagined as fabric: pull it too hard and it rips, exactly like cloth.
senses.whyCN: 身体组织被想象成布料：拉得太猛就会撕裂，正如撕布一样。

senses.title: To remove something quickly and roughly
senses.definition: to remove or detach something quickly and roughly, often off a surface or from its place
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而用力地把某物从表面或原处扯下、摘下
senses.example: She tore the poster off the wall and crumpled it.
senses.exampleCN: 她把海报从墙上扯下来揉成一团。
senses.why: The same separating force as sense 02 is applied to objects fixed in place: rip it free.
senses.whyCN: 与第 02 义项同一种分离之力，用在固定在原处的物体上：把它扯下来。

senses.title: To move very fast and wildly
senses.definition: to move somewhere very quickly, in a hurried or uncontrolled way
senses.definitionCN: 以匆忙、失控般的速度快速移动
senses.example: The kids tore down the hallway to answer the doorbell.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们沿着走廊飞奔过去开门。
senses.why: The violent, sweeping motion of ripping is transferred to a body rushing through space.
senses.whyCN: 撕裂时那种猛烈扫过的动作，被转移为身体在空间里横冲直撞。

senses.title: A hole or split in material
senses.definition: a hole or line of damage made in cloth, paper, or other material by ripping
senses.definitionCN: 布、纸等材料被撕开后留下的破洞或裂口
senses.example: There was a long tear in the sleeve of his jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他夹克的袖子上有一道长长的裂口。
senses.why: The result of the action in sense 02 hardens into a thing: the rip itself becomes a noun.
senses.whyCN: 第 02 义项动作的结果凝固成物：撕出来的那道口子成了名词。

senses.title: To be torn between two choices
senses.titleCN: 左右为难；在两者间纠结
senses.definition: to be unable to decide between two things because both feel important
senses.definitionCN: 因两个选择都很重要而无法决定、内心撕扯
senses.example: He was torn between staying with his family and taking the job abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他纠结于是留在家陪家人，还是出国接受那份工作。
senses.why: The mind is pictured as cloth being pulled from both ends until it almost splits.
senses.whyCN: 内心被画成一块两头受拉的布，几乎要被扯裂，故为两难。

senses.title: To destroy a relationship or group from within
senses.definition: to damage or destroy a relationship, family, or group by pulling its members apart
senses.definitionCN: 把关系、家庭或团体里的成员硬生生拆散、破坏
senses.example: The dispute over money tore the family apart.
senses.exampleCN: 金钱纠纷使这个家庭四分五裂。
senses.why: Abstract bonds are treated as fabric: force applied from inside rips the whole into pieces.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的关系被当作布料：来自内部的力量把整体撕成碎片。

intro.en: Tear is a doublet story: the noun and the verb look identical but come from two different ancient roots that met again in Old English.
intro.cn: tear 是一个「同形异源」的故事：名词与动词拼写相同，却来自两个不同的古老词根，在古英语中再次相遇。

items.en: The noun is generally traced to the reconstructed root *dakru-, the same ancient word that gave Greek dakry and Latin lacrima, all meaning 'tear'.
items.cn: 名词一般认为可追溯到重构词根 *dakru-，与希腊语 dakry、拉丁语 lacrima 同源，均表示「眼泪」。

items.en: In prehistoric Germanic, *dakru- underwent the regular sound shift and became *tahr-, inherited directly by Old English.
items.cn: 在史前日耳曼语中，*dakru- 经历了规律的音变，变为 *tahr-，被古英语直接继承。

items.en: Old English had the noun tear (tēar, 'tear drop') and, from a separate root *der- meaning 'to split or flay', the strong verb teran 'to tear'.
items.cn: 古英语中既有名词 tēar（泪滴），又有来自另一个词根 *der-（意为劈开、剥皮）的强变化动词 teran（撕）。

items.en: Middle English kept both words, spelled teere and teren, and the two spellings gradually converged into one modern form.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这两个词，拼作 teere 和 teren，两种拼写逐渐合流为现代的同一形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps the homographs apart in speech: the noun is pronounced with /ɪə/, the verb with /eə/, so listeners always know which root is meant.
items.cn: 现代英语在口语中以读音区分同形词：名词读 /ɪə/，动词读 /eə/，听者总能分辨指的是哪个来源。

note.en: Watch the two pronunciations, and separate the noun family (drops of water) from the verb family (ripping force).
note.cn: 注意两种读音，把「水滴家族」（名词）与「撕扯家族」（动词）分开理解。

entries.definition: full of tears; crying or likely to cry
entries.definitionCN: 含泪的；哭泣或快要哭出来的，由名词 tear 派生

entries.definition: wet with or having tears in the eyes
entries.definitionCN: 眼泪汪汪的，与 tearful 近义但更口语化

entries.definition: a single drop of tear, or anything shaped like one
entries.definitionCN: 一滴泪；泪滴状的东西，由 tear 与 drop 复合而成

entries.definition: a film or story deliberately made to make people cry
entries.definitionCN: 催人泪下的电影或故事，属口语复合词

entries.definition: the past participle of the verb tear, also used as an adjective
entries.definitionCN: 动词 tear 的过去分词，也可作形容词表示「撕裂的；纠结的」

entries.definition: to tear something quickly and roughly, often along a line
entries.definitionCN: 迅速用力地撕开，与动词 tear 近义但更强调干脆利落

entries.definition: to divide something into two or more parts, often along a natural line
entries.definitionCN: 把某物分成两半或多份，常指顺纹理分开

entries.definition: to tear something violently into pieces, now rare and literary
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈地撕碎，现多见于文学语体，与 tear 同源于古义

entries.definition: to cry, especially in a quiet or prolonged way
entries.definitionCN: 哭泣，尤指安静或长时间的流泪，比 cry 更正式

entries.definition: to cry noisily while taking short, sudden breaths
entries.definitionCN: 抽泣；呜咽，强调伴随抽噎的哭法

normalIntro.en: Five anchors built from the word's real roots, forms, and collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自该词真实的词根、变形与搭配。

normal.en: Noun tear rhymes with 'ear': tears come from near the ears of the face, the eyes.
normal.cn: 名词 tear 与 ear 押韵：泪水和耳朵一样都长在脸上，联想「脸上有 ear 就有 tear」。

normal.en: Verb tear rhymes with 'air': rip a page off and let it fly into the air.
normal.cn: 动词 tear 与 air 押韵：把一页纸撕下来，让它飞进空气里。

normal.en: Past forms run tore → torn: the paper was torn apart, the team was torn apart.
normal.cn: 过去式 tore、过去分词 torn：纸被 torn apart，家庭也可能被 torn apart。

normal.en: The family set is tearful, teary, teardrop, tearless: tear + -ful / -y / drop / -less.
normal.cn: 词族一串记：tearful（含泪的）、teary（泪汪汪的）、teardrop（泪珠）、tearless（无泪的）。

normal.en: burst into tears and in tears are the fixed collocations for starting to cry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配记两头：burst into tears（突然大哭）、in tears（含着泪）。

abstract.en: Picture one water drop sliding from an eye, then picture two hands pulling a sheet of paper apart.
abstract.cn: 画面一：一滴水从眼角滑落；画面二：两只手把一张纸撕成两半。

abstract.en: Feel the muscle in your leg as fabric: stretch it too far and it rips like cloth.
abstract.cn: 把腿部肌肉想象成布料：拉过头了，就会像布一样撕裂开来。

abstract.en: Being torn between two doors: one rope pulls you left, another pulls you right.
abstract.cn: 纠结即撕扯：两扇门各拴一根绳，一根拉你向左，一根拉你向右。

examples.en: A tear rolled down his cheek as he said goodbye.
examples.cn: 他说再见时，一滴泪从脸颊滑落。

examples.en: Do not tear the package; cut it open with scissors.
examples.cn: 别把包裹撕开，用剪刀剪开。

examples.en: She was torn between two offers and could not sleep for days.
examples.cn: 她在两个录用通知之间纠结，好几天睡不好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「梯尔」——踩空梯子摔下来，又疼又委屈：疼得流泪读 /tɪə/，裤子摔破读 /teə/。一个音流泪，一个音撕布。

root: 同形异源双词根：名词 tear 来自古英语 tēar，一般认为源自印欧词根 *dakru-（与拉丁语 lacrima「泪」同源）；动词 tear 来自古英语 teran，源自印欧词根 *der-（劈开、剥开）。两词只是拼写巧合相同，词义系统各自独立。

sensesIntro.en: One spelling covers two roots: senses about drops of water grow from the noun root, while senses about force and damage grow from the verb root.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个拼写覆盖两个来源：与水滴相关的义项长自名词词根，与用力、破坏相关的义项长自动词词根。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: A DROP FROM THE EYE, AND CLOTH PULLED APART BY FORCE
core.cn: 核心意象：从眼角滴落的水珠，和被双手撕开的布

branches.en: MOISTURE AND EMOTION: the drop that feeling pushes out of the eye
branches.cn: 水分与情绪：情感把水从眼里推出来的那一滴

branches.en: RUPTURE AND FORCE: hands ripping paper, tearing posters off walls
branches.cn: 破裂与用力：双手撕纸、把海报从墙上扯下

branches.en: DAMAGE IN THE BODY: muscle and ligament treated as fabric that can rip
branches.cn: 身体损伤：肌肉韧带被当作可能撕裂的布料

branches.en: THE RIP AS RESULT AND AS CONFLICT: the hole left behind, the mind pulled both ways
branches.cn: 破口作为结果与冲突：留下的裂口，被两头拉扯的心

branches.en: URGENCY AND BREAKDOWN: bodies rushing like torn wind, groups ripped from inside
branches.cn: 疾奔与瓦解：人如狂风般飞奔，团体从内部被撕裂

intro.en: Tear builds a small but regular family: suffixes attach mostly to the noun root, and the verb contributes its participle torn.
intro.cn: tear 的构词家族不大但很规整：后缀多挂在名词词根上，动词则贡献过去分词 torn。

latinIntro.en: Through the shared root *dakru-, tear has Latin relatives built on lacrima, the classical word for a tear.
latinIntro.cn: 经由共同词根 *dakru-，tear 在拉丁语中的同族词围绕 lacrima（古典语中的「泪」）构成。

definition_zh: 偏爱；优先；优待；优先权
definition_en: the choosing of one thing over another, or the right to be served or paid before others
core_image: 一只盘子里的两块点心本一模一样，拿筷子的人却每次都先夹靠左那一块，动作快得像是早已决定
scene: 早上七点，车站售票窗口前拉起了两列队伍，戴徽章的工作人员把一侧的人先引到柜台前。 Give your preference to families with small children when seats are limited.
sceneCN: 这里本词指优先安排或优先照顾（第 2 个义项：把先办、先得的次序给别人）；句意为座位有限时优先安排带幼儿的家庭；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 偏爱；更喜欢的事物（可数或不可数）

由同族动词加表「可……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为「更可取的」

senses.title: Liking one thing more
senses.definition: a stronger liking for one thing than for another
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的喜欢超过对另一物的喜欢
senses.example: Her preference is for strong tea rather than coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 她偏爱浓茶而非咖啡。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to carry a thing in front; what is put in front is what one favours.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为把某物搬到前面；被放到前面，就是被偏爱的。

senses.title: The right to be served first
senses.definition: the right or practice of being dealt with before others
senses.definitionCN: 先于他人得到办理或照顾的权利或做法
senses.example: Give your preference to families with small children when seats are limited.
senses.exampleCN: 座位有限时优先安排带幼儿的家庭。
senses.why: Being placed before others is a literal carrying forward, so the noun marks rank as well as taste.
senses.whyCN: 被放在他人之前，正是字面意义上的搬到前面，因此该名词也标出次序。

senses.title: A trade advantage
senses.definition: a lower tariff or easier terms granted to certain trading partners
senses.definitionCN: 给予某些贸易伙伴的较低关税或更宽条件
senses.example: The agreement grants tariff preference to the smallest exporters.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议给予最小规模的出口商关税优惠。
senses.why: A partner carried to the front of the queue is a partner who pays less at the border.
senses.whyCN: 被提到队伍前面的伙伴，就是在关境上付款更少的伙伴。

senses.title: A first claim in law
senses.definition: the right of one creditor to be paid before others from a debtor's property
senses.definitionCN: 某一债权人从债务人财产中先于他人受偿的权利
senses.example: The bank's preference over the land was recorded at the registry.
senses.exampleCN: 银行对这块地的优先受偿权已在登记处记录。
senses.why: Law keeps the order of payment literal: one claim is carried ahead of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 法律把付款次序说得很字面：一项债权被搬到其余债权之前。

senses.title: One's first choice
senses.definition: the person or thing one would choose first if only one could be had
senses.definitionCN: 若只能得到一个，会最先选择的人或物
senses.example: This route is our preference for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路线是我们过河的首选。
senses.why: Choosing is ranking, and the top of the ranking is what stands in front.
senses.whyCN: 选择就是排序，排在最前面的那一个就是被放到前面的。

senses.title: Settings stored by software
senses.definition: stored choices that tell a program how its user wants it to behave
senses.definitionCN: 程序记录下来的、说明用户希望它如何运作的选择
senses.example: The app keeps your preference even after you sign out.
senses.exampleCN: 即使退出登录，这款应用仍保留你的偏好设置。
senses.why: A machine that remembers a choice keeps a small record of what its user put first.
senses.whyCN: 会记住选择机器，就是留下用户「把什么放在前面」的小记录。

senses.title: A pattern in buying
senses.definition: the tendency of buyers to favour certain goods, brands or features
senses.definitionCN: 购买者更偏爱某些商品、品牌或特性的趋势
senses.example: Surveys track preference for local produce.
senses.exampleCN: 调查追踪消费者对本地农产品的偏好。
senses.why: Economists widen one person's taste into a measurable pattern of favouring.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把一个人的口味扩展成可测量的偏爱模式。

senses.title: A taste shaped by culture
senses.definition: a leaning in style, art or custom that a group learns rather than inherits
senses.definitionCN: 群体习得而非天生继承的风格、艺术或习俗上的偏向
senses.example: Colour preference varies sharply between regions.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色偏好在不同地区差别很大。
senses.why: Shared leaning is still a carrying forward of one option, only now by a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 共享的偏向仍然是「把某一选项搬到前面」，只是搬运者换成了一个群体。

intro.en: Preference comes from Latin praeferre 'to carry in front, place before', built from prae- 'before' and ferre 'to carry'; English took it through French.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语 praeferre「搬到前面、置于前面」，由表「在前」的前缀加 ferre「携带」构成；英语经法语借入。

items.en: Ferre meant 'to carry, bear, bring', one of the most common verbs of movement in Latin.
items.cn: ferre 意为「携带、承载、带来」，是拉丁语中最常见的移动动词之一。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front', whether of place or of rank.
items.cn: 表「在前」的前缀意为在位置上或次序上靠前。

items.en: Praeferre joined the two: to carry something in front of something else, hence to set one above another.
items.cn: 两相结合构成的动词意为把某物搬到另一物之前，因此引申为把某物排到另一物之上。

items.en: French made a noun of the verb, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century for the act of favouring.
items.cn: 法语把该动词名词化，英语在十四世纪借入，指偏爱的行为。

items.en: Courts and merchants narrowed the noun to a right of first payment and a lower tariff.
items.cn: 法庭与商人把该名词收窄为先受偿的权利与更低的关税。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is placed in the fourteenth century, and the older base behind ferre is generally considered a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语最早书证定于十四世纪，而 ferre 背后的更早词基一般认为是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close and are often confused with this noun; group two holds words for choosing and for liking.
note.cn: 第一组是与本词形近或音近、常被混淆的词；第二组是表示选择与喜爱的词。

entries.definition: The base verb meaning to like one thing better; the noun adds the result of that liking.
entries.definitionCN: 基干动词，意为更喜欢某物；名词则加出这种喜爱的结果。

entries.definition: The adjective built on this noun, describing treatment that gives someone first place.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词构成的形容词，描述给予某人优先地位的处理方式。

entries.definition: A noun for advancement in office, from the same verb but with a different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该动词，但指职位上的升迁，义项不同。

entries.definition: An adjective saying one option is better; it evaluates rather than records a taste.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，表示某个选项更好；它作评价，而不记录口味。

entries.definition: The act of picking or the set of options; preference is the leaning that guides the pick.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选的动作或可选范围；本词是引导挑选的那种偏向。

entries.definition: Simple fondness for something, without the sense of ranking one above another.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的朴素喜爱，不含把某物排在另一物之上的意味。

entries.definition: The state of coming first because of urgency or importance, a matter of order rather than taste.
entries.definitionCN: 因紧急或重要而排在最前，讲的是次序而非口味。

entries.definition: A favourable condition or benefit; the trade sense of preference is one kind of advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 有利条件或好处；本词的贸易义是其中一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two real parts: a prefix meaning before, and a verb meaning to carry.
normal.cn: 两个真实成分：一个表「在前」的前缀，加一个表「携带」的动词。

normal.en: The family runs prefer, preference, preferable, preferably, preferential.
normal.cn: 同族词包括更喜欢、偏爱、更可取的、最好是、优先的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: have a preference for, give preference to, in preference to.
normal.cn: 固定说法：偏爱、优先考虑、优先于。

normal.en: Every technical use puts somebody at the front: a creditor, an exporter, a passenger, a setting.
normal.cn: 每个专业用法都把某一方放到前面：债权人、出口商、乘客、某项设置。

normal.en: The noun records a ranking; the verb records the act of ranking.
normal.cn: 名词记录的是排序结果，动词记录的是排序的动作。

abstract.en: Picture two identical cakes on a plate and a hand that always reaches left first.
abstract.cn: 想象盘里两块一模一样的点心，一只手每次都先伸向左边。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid across a queue to mark who is let through first.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳子横在队伍中，标出谁先被放行。

abstract.en: Picture a screen that remembers which button you press every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一块屏幕记住了你每天早上按的那个按钮。

examples.en: He has a strong preference for quiet rooms.
examples.cn: 他非常偏爱安静的房间。

examples.en: Preference was given to applicants from the region.
examples.cn: 优先考虑了来自本地区的申请人。

examples.en: You can change your preference at any time.
examples.cn: 你随时可以更改自己的偏好设置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「在前」与「携带」合起来看：把某样东西搬到前面，就是偏爱它、优先待它。

root: 拉丁 praeferre「搬到前面、置于前面」＝表「在前」的前缀＋ferre「携带」；英语经法语借入，由「置于前」引申为偏爱与优先；更深词基一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: an object carried to the front is the one liked, served first, taxed less, paid first, chosen first, remembered by a machine, favoured by buyers and shaped by a culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：被搬到前面的东西，就是被偏爱的、先被服务的、少缴税的、先受偿的、首选中的、被机器记住的、被买家青睐的、被文化塑造的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical cakes on a plate, and a hand that always reaches for the left one first.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘里两块一模一样的点心，一只手每次都先伸向左边的。

branches.en: TASTE AND CULTURE: one person's liking and a region's shared style are the same favouring at two scales.
branches.cn: 口味与文化：一个人的喜爱与一个地区共享的风格，是同一种偏爱在两个尺度上。

branches.en: RANK AND TRADE: being served before others and paying less at the border both mean being moved ahead.
branches.cn: 次序与贸易：先被服务与在关境少缴税，都意味着被移到前面。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CLAIM: a creditor carried ahead of the rest keeps the image in strict order.
branches.cn: 法律的求偿：被搬到其余人之前的债权人，把这意象保持在严格次序里。

branches.en: THE FIRST CHOICE: what one would pick first stands at the head of a ranking.
branches.cn: 首选：最先会挑的那个，排在名单的最前。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MARKET: a stored setting and a buyer's pattern both record what is put first.
branches.cn: 机器与市场：存下的设置与买家的模式，都记录「什么被放在前面」。

intro.en: Preference is a Latin noun formed from a prefix, a carrying verb and a noun suffix; the same pieces build a small English family, so the word can be read in parts.
intro.cn: 本词是由表方向的前缀、表「携带」的动词与名词后缀构成的拉丁名词；同样的部件构成一个小英语词族，可按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- supplies 'before' and ferre supplies 'carry'; the noun suffix names the act, and English adds nothing further.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「在前」的前缀提供「之前」之义，表「携带」的动词提供搬运义，名词后缀命名这一行为；英语不再加缀。

items.example: The verb is the carrying itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词就是「搬」这个动作本身。

items.meaning: to carry in front, to set above
items.example: To carry a thing in front is to give it the first place.
items.exampleCN: 把东西搬到前面，就是给它第一位。

items.example: The state noun named the favouring.
items.exampleCN: 这个状态名词命名偏爱。

items.meaning: a liking, or a right to come first
items.example: Her preference is for the coast road.
Bring a map, preferably a paper one.
items.exampleCN: 带张地图，最好是纸质的。
这家公司赢得了优待条件。

items.meaning: a share paid before ordinary shares

definition_zh: 倾向；有…趋势；趋向；照料；照看；管理；在酒吧当班；放牧；（古）侍候
definition_en: to be likely to do something or to move in a certain direction; to take care of someone or something
core_image: 水往低处流，而牧人低头跟着羊群往坡下走
scene: 每到冬天，他的咳嗽就更厉害。 Every winter his cough tends to get worse, and the doctor says the cold air is the cause.
sceneCN: 这里 tend 是「倾向于、有…趋势」（第 1 个义项：经常如此或很可能如此）；句意：每年冬天他的咳嗽都倾向于加重，医生说是冷空气刺激。图中可辨识物件：病历、冬季窗景、雾化器、围巾、医生的听诊器。

pos.zh: 倾向；趋向；照料；照看；管理；当班

derivatives.zh: 倾向；趋势
照料；护理
有倾向性的；带偏见的
照料者；温柔的（同根近亲，义已分化）

senses.title: Be likely to do something
senses.definition: to be likely to do or be something, as a regular pattern
senses.definitionCN: 经常如此或很可能如此
senses.example: People tend to ignore warnings they hear too often.
senses.exampleCN: 人们倾向于忽略听太多的警告。
senses.why: Tendere means 'to stretch'. The modern sense pictures behaviour stretched toward one outcome: the pattern leans, and prediction follows the lean.
senses.whyCN: tendere 意为“伸展”。现代义把行为想象为朝某个结果伸展：模式倾斜，预测随倾斜而来。

senses.title: Take care of someone
senses.definition: to look after a person, especially one who is ill or young
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人，尤指病者或幼者
senses.example: Nurses tended the wounded through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 护士整夜照料伤员。
senses.why: This sense has a different parent: it is a shortened form of attend, 'to direct one's mind to'. Care is attention made practical.
senses.whyCN: 此义另有来源：它是 attend“把心思朝向”的缩略。照料是“注意”被付诸实践。

senses.title: Move in a direction
senses.definition: to move or point toward a place or state
senses.definitionCN: 朝某处或某状态移动、指向
senses.example: The path tends toward the river.
senses.exampleCN: 小径趋向河边。
senses.why: The spatial sense is the most literal: a line or a road stretches in a direction. Inclination in behaviour is this stretching made mental.
senses.whyCN: 空间义最字面：一条线或路朝某方向伸展。行为上的倾向，就是这种伸展被心智化。

senses.title: Have an inclination of opinion
senses.definition: to be inclined to hold a view or favour an option
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于持有某观点或支持某选项
senses.example: The committee tends toward a compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于妥协。
senses.why: Opinions also lean. The verb lets a speaker report a drift without claiming a fixed position: the group is not there yet, but it is tending there.
senses.whyCN: 观点也会倾斜。动词让说话者报告一种漂移而不宣称固定立场：群体尚未到达，但正朝那里去。

senses.title: Look after a fire or machine
senses.definition: to keep a fire, machine, or process working properly
senses.definitionCN: 使炉火、机器或过程正常运转
senses.example: He tended the furnace all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他整夜照看炉子。
senses.why: Tending a fire is maintenance as attention: add fuel, watch the draft, respond to changes. The cared-for object is not alive, but it needs vigilance.
senses.whyCN: 照看炉火是“注意”式的维护：添燃料、看通风、应对变化。被照看之物并非活物，却需要警觉。

senses.title: Serve in a bar
senses.definition: to work behind a bar, serving drinks
senses.definitionCN: 在吧台后工作、供应饮品
senses.example: She tends bar on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 她周末在酒吧当班。
senses.why: American English uses tend for a workplace one keeps running. The bartender tends the bar as a shepherd tends a flock: presence plus upkeep.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语用 tend 指维持一个工作场所运转。酒吧侍者 tend 吧台，如牧人 tend 羊群：在场加维护。

senses.title: Herd animals
senses.definition: to watch over animals as they graze
senses.definitionCN: 看管吃草的牲畜
senses.example: A boy tended the goats on the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 一个男孩在山坡上放羊。
senses.why: Herding is the oldest care sense: the animals move, and the herder's attention moves with them, keeping them from straying.
senses.whyCN: 放牧是最古老的照料义：牲畜移动，牧人的注意力随之前移，防止它们走失。

senses.title: Attend or wait upon (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to attend on a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：随侍地位高者
senses.example: The squire tended his lord.
senses.exampleCN: 侍从随侍他的领主。
senses.why: This is the attend branch in its full feudal form: standing ready, mind directed toward the master's needs. Modern care kept the service and dropped the rank.
senses.whyCN: 这是 attend 一支的完整封建形态：立于一旁待命，心思朝向主人的需要。现代“照料”保留服侍，丢掉等级。

senses.title: Converge on a result
senses.definition: of numbers or processes, to approach a limit or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 数字或过程逼近某一极限或结果
senses.example: Under these rules, costs tend toward zero.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些规则下，成本趋于零。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the spatial lean for convergence: a sequence stretches toward a limit it may never reach exactly.
senses.whyCN: 数学用空间倾斜表示收敛：序列朝一个可能永远不能精确到达的极限伸展。

intro.en: English has two tend verbs that now look alike. The 'incline' tend comes from Old French tendre, Latin tendere 'to stretch'. The 'care for' tend is a shortened form of attend, from Old French atendre, Latin attendere 'to give heed'. They merged in spelling but not in origin.
intro.cn: 英语有两个现已形似的 tend 动词。“倾向”的 tend 出自古法语 tendre、拉丁 tendere“伸展”；“照料”的 tend 是 attend 的缩略，出自古法语 atendre、拉丁 attendere“留心”。它们在拼写上合并，来源却不同。

items.en: The 'stretch, incline' verb enters English from Old French tendre, used of movement and direction.
items.cn: “伸展、倾向”动词十三世纪自法语 tendre 进入英语，用于移动与方向。

items.en: tendere means 'to stretch, extend, direct'. Its past participle tensus gives tense and tension.
items.cn: tendere 意为“伸展、延伸、指向”。其过去分词 tensus 生成 tense 与 tension。

items.en: tendere is traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch', the same root behind tendon and the ten- of intend and extend.
items.cn: tendere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”，同一词根见于 tendon，以及 intend、extend 中的 ten-。

items.en: The 'care for' sense comes from attend, 'to direct the mind to', later shortened to tend in everyday use.
items.cn: “照料”义出自 attend“把心思朝向”，后在日常使用中缩略为 tend。

items.en: attendere is ad- 'to' plus tendere 'stretch': to stretch one's mind toward something. So care and inclination are distant cousins after all.
items.cn: attendere 是 ad-“朝向”加 tendere“伸展”：把心思朝某物伸去。故“照料”与“倾向”终究是远亲。

items.en: Modern English keeps both: tend to do (incline) and tend a fire (care for). Context, not spelling, tells them apart.
items.cn: 现代英语两者皆存：tend to do（倾向）与 tend a fire（照看）。区分靠语境，不靠拼写。

note.en: The first group is the tend family and its look-alikes; the second is verbs that share either the leaning or the caring sense.
note.cn: 第一组是 tend 词族与形近词；第二组是共享“倾斜”或“照料”义的动词。

entries.definition: a regular inclination to behave in a certain way.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式行事的经常性倾向。

entries.definition: expressing a strong biased point of view. It comes from German Tendenz, not directly from English tend.
entries.definitionCN: 表达强烈偏见的。出自德语 Tendenz，并非直接来自英语 tend。

entries.definition: looking after; the act of caring for.
entries.definitionCN: 照看；照料的行为。

entries.definition: to lean or be disposed toward something. It is more formal and more spatial than tend.
entries.definitionCN: 向某物倾斜或有意向。比 tend 更正式、更空间化。

entries.definition: to look after someone's needs. It is the plain phrase for the 'tend' care sense.
entries.definitionCN: 照看某人的需要。是“照料”义的朴素说法。

entries.definition: to be drawn toward something as if by gravity. It stresses attraction rather than habit.
entries.definitionCN: 如受重力吸引般趋向某物。强调吸引而非习惯。

normalIntro.en: Real links: tendere 'stretch', attend shortened to tend, the tense/tension family, and the two-verb history.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tendere“伸展”、attend 缩略为 tend、tense 与 tension 词族，以及“双动词”历史。

normal.en: Tendere means 'stretch'. Behaviour tends when it stretches toward one outcome rather than another.
normal.cn: tendere 意为“伸展”。行为 tend，就是朝某个结果而非另一个伸展。

normal.en: The care sense is attend shortened: to tend a patient is to stretch your attention toward them.
normal.cn: 照料义是 attend 的缩略：tend 病人，就是把注意力朝他们伸去。

normal.en: Tend, tense, tension, tendon all go back to stretching. A tendon is a stretched cord.
normal.cn: tend、tense、tension、tendon 都回到“伸展”。肌腱就是一根被拉紧的索。

normal.en: Tend to do = habit leans; tend a fire = attention stays. Context decides which verb you met.
normal.cn: tend to do 是习惯倾斜；tend a fire 是注意力留守。语境决定你遇到哪一个。

normal.en: Intend and extend hide the same ten-: stretching the mind toward, or stretching out.
normal.cn: intend 与 extend 藏着同一个 ten-：把心思伸向，或向外伸展。

abstract.en: A tendency is a future written into the present as a slope; tend names the slope without promising the destination.
abstract.cn: 倾向是写进当下的未来，形如斜坡；tend 命名坡度，却不承诺终点。

abstract.en: Care and inclination meet in attention: both are a stretching of the self toward something beyond it.
abstract.cn: 照料与倾向在“注意”处相遇：两者都是自我朝外物的伸展。

abstract.en: What we tend grows; what we merely intend does not. The hand matters more than the plan.
abstract.cn: 我们所照料的东西会生长；仅仅所意图的不会。手比计划更重要。

examples.en: Prices tend to rise before the holiday.
examples.cn: 节前价格往往上涨。

examples.en: A nurse tended him through the night.
examples.cn: 一名护士整夜照料他。

examples.en: The discussion tended toward the question of cost.
examples.cn: 讨论逐渐转向成本问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “探的”——探着身子往一个方向去，也探身照看病人 → tend 倾向、照料

root: 两个来源合流：“倾向”义出自拉丁 tendere“伸展”（经古法语 tendre）；“照料”义是 attend 的缩略，出自拉丁 attendere“留心”（ad- + tendere）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of tend, split between two histories: a stretching toward (inclination, direction, convergence) and an attention turned toward (care, herding, service). Both are forms of leaning out of oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: tend 的九个义项分属两段历史：朝某物伸展（倾向、方向、收敛）与把注意转向某物（照料、放牧、服侍）。两者都是自我向外倾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line stretched toward a point, and a herder's gaze stretched toward a flock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条朝某点伸展的线，与牧人朝羊群伸去的目光。

branches.en: HABIT: behaviour leans in a predictable direction.
branches.cn: 习惯：行为朝可预测的方向倾斜。

branches.en: DIRECTION AND LIMIT: paths and sequences stretch toward a point.
branches.cn: 方向与极限：路径与序列朝某点伸展。

branches.en: CARE: attention is turned toward a person, a fire, or a machine that needs upkeep.
branches.cn: 照料：注意力转向需要维护的人、炉火或机器。

branches.en: SERVICE: bars, flocks, and lords are all kept by a presence that stays.
branches.cn: 服侍：酒吧、羊群与领主，都靠一种留守的在场维持。

branches.en: THE UNFINISHED MIND: a group can tend toward a view without having reached it.
branches.cn: 未完成的心智：群体可以趋向某观点而尚未抵达。

intro.en: Tend's English family splits along its two origins: tendency belongs to the 'stretch' verb, while attend and its derivatives belong to the 'heed' verb. The ten- root also gives tense, tension, tendon, intend, and extend.
intro.cn: tend 的英语词族沿两个来源分裂：tendency 属“伸展”动词，attend 及其派生属“留心”动词。ten- 词根还给出 tense、tension、tendon、intend、extend。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere 'stretch' has the participle tensus, source of tense and tension. Latin attendere 'stretch toward' is ad- plus tendere, and its French shortening gave the care sense of tend. The same *ten- root underlies tendon.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tendere“伸展”的分词 tensus 是 tense 与 tension 的来源。拉丁 attendere“朝…伸展”是 ad- 加 tendere，其法语缩略给出 tend 的照料义。同一 *ten- 词根支撑 tendon。

definition_zh: 不可避免地；必然地；势必；无法阻止地
definition_en: in a way that cannot be avoided or prevented
core_image: 一块裂开的石碑，裂缝从顶端一路向下延伸，无法停住
scene: 仓库里的货架只用几根细木条支撑，管理员在巡检记录里写下判断。 With such thin supports, the shelf will inevitably give way under the weight.
sceneCN: 这里指人力无法阻止的结局（第 2 个义项：无法阻止地）；句意为支撑太细，这个货架在重压下必然垮掉。

pos.zh: 不可避免地；必然地；势必

derivatives.zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的
必然性；不可避免
不可避免的性质（较少用）

senses.title: The announced certainty
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to present a result as the predictable outcome of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，把随后的结果说成前情注定会带来的结局
senses.example: Inevitably, the discussion drifted back to the same old argument.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论不可避免地又绕回那个老话题。
senses.why: As a sentence adverb it colours the whole clause rather than one verb, telling the reader that the outcome was already settled.
senses.whyCN: 作为句子副词，它修饰整个小句而不是单个动词，向读者暗示结局早已注定。

senses.title: No one can stop it
senses.definition: in a way that cannot be prevented by any person or effort
senses.definitionCN: 以任何人都无法阻止的方式
senses.example: With such thin supports, the shelf will inevitably give way under the weight.
senses.exampleCN: 支撑太细，这个货架在重压下必然会垮。
senses.why: Placed before the verb, it claims practical impossibility rather than mere probability.
senses.whyCN: 放在动词前时，它说的是现实中办不到，而不只是可能性很大。

senses.title: Logical consequence
senses.definition: as a conclusion that must follow from the stated premises
senses.definitionCN: 作为由既定前提必然推出的结论
senses.example: If every premise is true, the conclusion follows inevitably.
senses.exampleCN: 如果每个前提都成立，结论就必然随之而来。
senses.why: In logic the word marks deductive necessity, a stronger claim than empirical likelihood.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑语境中它标记演绎必然性，比经验上的可能性更强。

senses.title: Not necessarily
senses.definition: used with a negative to deny that one thing must lead to another
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，否认一件事必定引出另一件事
senses.example: A wealthy country is not inevitably a peaceful one.
senses.exampleCN: 富裕的国家未必就是和平的国家。
senses.why: Under negation the word stops asserting necessity; the sentence says the link is avoidable, not that it never occurs.
senses.whyCN: 在否定句中它不再断言必然，句子说的是这条联系可以避免，而不是从不发生。

senses.title: As always happens
senses.definition: used of a repeated event that experience makes predictable
senses.definitionCN: 用于经验上早已可料的重复事件
senses.example: As inevitably happens at long meetings, someone raised the coffee question.
senses.exampleCN: 正如长会上一贯会发生的那样，有人提起了咖啡的问题。
senses.why: The habitual frame turns inevitability into a comment on human routine, often with a touch of resignation.
senses.whyCN: 习惯性框架把必然转成对人世间惯例的评注，常带一点无奈。

senses.title: Coupled with something
senses.definition: used before a past participle to say that two things always come together
senses.definitionCN: 放在过去分词前，表示两件事总是同时出现
senses.example: Rapid expansion is inevitably accompanied by administrative strain.
senses.exampleCN: 快速扩张必然伴随行政上的紧绷。
senses.why: Here it modifies a participle rather than a finite verb, describing an inseparable pairing rather than one future event.
senses.whyCN: 这里修饰分词而非限定动词，描述的是不可分离的伴随关系，而不是某一件将来的事。

senses.title: The formal claim of a law
senses.definition: in academic or formal prose, used to present a general rule as beyond exception
senses.definitionCN: 在学术或正式散文中，把一般规律说成没有例外
senses.example: Any measure of this kind inevitably raises questions about privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这类措施必然引发关于隐私的疑问。
senses.why: The formal register uses the adverb as a rhetorical seal, claiming a general law rather than predicting one case.
senses.whyCN: 正式语域把它当作修辞上的封印，声称的是一条普遍规律，而不是预测某一次情形。

senses.title: Unavoidably incurred
senses.titleCN: 过程中无法免除的代价
senses.definition: used of costs or losses that must be accepted in a process
senses.definitionCN: 用于某个过程中必须承受的成本或损耗
senses.example: Some loss of detail is inevitably incurred when a file is compressed.
senses.exampleCN: 压缩文件时，细节的损失是无法免除的。
senses.why: Technical writing uses the word for unavoidable by-products of a procedure, where no agent is to blame.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作里它指程序中无法避免的副产物，并不归咎于某个人。

intro.en: Inevitably comes from the Latin adjective for unavoidable plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词的直接来源很清楚：拉丁语「不可回避的」形容词加英语副词后缀。只有英语首见年代是约数，不构成来源争议。

items.en: The verb vitare means to shun or avoid, and it supplies the core of the later adjective.
items.cn: 动词意为「躲开、回避」，为后来的形容词提供词干。

items.en: The prefix e-, meaning out, plus vitare forms evitabilis, that which can be avoided.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀与「回避」合成「可以躲开的」。

items.en: The negating prefix in- turns evitabilis into inevitabilis, that which cannot be avoided.
items.cn: 否定前缀加在「可以躲开的」上，得到「躲不开的」。

items.en: French inévitable and English inevitable carry the adjective into general use; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 法语与英语的形容词把这一说法带入通用语；英语首见年代只是约数。

items.en: English adds its adverb suffix to the adjective, and the new form takes over the sentence-initial role.
items.cn: 英语在形容词上加副词后缀，这个新形式随后承担句首评注功能。

items.en: Modern usage spreads from fatalistic speech to technical and academic claims of necessity.
items.cn: 现代用法从宿命式口语扩展到技术与学术上的必然性断言。

note.en: The first group belongs to the same Latin avoid-root family; the second group names ways of saying that something cannot be escaped.
note.cn: 第一组同属拉丁语「回避」词族；第二组是表达「逃不掉」的近义说法。

entries.definition: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 必定发生且无法避免的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The quality of being impossible to avoid.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免的性质；必然性。

entries.definition: Able to be avoided; rare, and formed without the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 可避免的；较少见，未带否定前缀。

entries.definition: The state of being unavoidable, a rarer noun than inevitability.
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免的状态，比必然性一词更少用。

entries.definition: As a logical or causal result that cannot be otherwise.
entries.definitionCN: 作为无法另作他解的逻辑或因果结果。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be avoided in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 在实际中无法避开地。

entries.definition: As an immediate result, without a separate decision or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 作为直接结果自动发生，无需另作决定或努力。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be escaped or resisted; literary and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 无法逃脱或抗拒地；书面而正式。

entries.definition: Because circumstances leave no other choice.
entries.definitionCN: 因情形所迫而没有别的选择。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real negative prefix, the real avoid-root and the real sentence patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的否定前缀、真实的「回避」词根与真实句式。

normal.en: The prefix means not and the root means avoid, so the word is simply cannot be avoided.
normal.cn: 前缀表示「不」，词根表示「避开」，合起来就是「躲不开」。

normal.en: Rain does not ask permission before falling, and that is the tone of this word.
normal.cn: 雨点落下前不会征求同意，这正是这个词的语气。

normal.en: Put it first in a sentence and the comma falls like a judge's gavel.
normal.cn: 把它放在句首，后面的逗号就像法槌落下。

normal.en: Under negation it retreats at once: not inevitable means only not necessarily.
normal.cn: 在否定句里它立刻退让：不是必然，只是未必。

normal.en: Engineering reports like it for costs that no procedure can remove.
normal.cn: 工程报告爱用它给无法免除的损耗定性。

abstract.en: Inevitability is not a prediction of a date but an admission that the end was written into the conditions.
abstract.cn: 必然不是预言某一天，而是承认结局早已写在条件里。

abstract.en: The feeling of inevitability comes from looking back, when every step seems to have had no alternative.
abstract.cn: 真正的必然感来自回头看，那时每一步都像没得选。

abstract.en: The adverb quietly moves responsibility away from people and onto the nature of things.
abstract.cn: 这个副词把责任从人身上悄悄拿走，交给事情本身。

examples.en: Inevitably, the first draft raised more questions than it answered.
examples.cn: 初稿不可避免地提出的问题多于它回答的问题。

examples.en: Without maintenance, the pipes will inevitably corrode.
examples.cn: 若不加维护，这些管道必然会被腐蚀。

examples.en: The report notes that some delay is inevitably incurred at every handover.
examples.cn: 报告指出，每次交接都不可避免地产生一些延误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因未特布利」——因为没能避开，所以必然发生

root: 拉丁语动词「回避」加表示「向外」的前缀构成「可避免的」，再加否定前缀成为「不可回避的」；英语由该形容词加副词后缀构成。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate sentence-level fatalism, practical impossibility, deductive necessity, negated necessity, habitual resignation, inseparable pairing, formal law-claims and unavoidable process costs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理句首宿命评注、现实中的无法阻止、演绎必然、被否定的必然、习惯性无奈、不可分离的伴随、书面规律断言，以及过程中无法免除的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cracked stone tablet whose fracture runs from top to bottom and cannot be halted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块裂开的石碑，裂缝从顶端一路向下，无法止住。

branches.en: THE ANNOUNCED OUTCOME: the sentence adverb that declares a result settled.
branches.cn: 宣布的结果：句首副词把结局说成已成定局。

branches.en: THE BLOCKED PATH: no person or effort can prevent it.
branches.cn: 被堵死的路：任何人、任何努力都挡不住。

branches.en: THE LAW-LIKE CLAIM: deductive necessity and the formal assertion of a general rule.
branches.cn: 近乎规律的断言：演绎必然后承与书面语中的一般规律。

branches.en: THE DENIED LINK: under negation the word means not necessarily.
branches.cn: 被否认的链条：在否定句中意为「未必」。

branches.en: THE ACCEPTED PRICE: habit, inseparable pairing and costs incurred by a process.
branches.cn: 接受的代价：习惯性重演、如影随形的伴随，以及过程无法免除的损耗。

intro.en: Inevitably is built from a Latin negative prefix, a Latin avoid-root, two Latin suffixes and an English adverb suffix; every part is transparent.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语否定前缀、「回避」词根、两个拉丁后缀与一个英语副词后缀构成，每个构件都清楚可辨。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family starts from the verb for shun and builds an adjective of possibility, which the negative prefix then reverses.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族从表示「回避」的动词出发，先构成表可能性的形容词，再由否定前缀把它反转。

items.example: The prefix reverses the possibility carried by the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把形容词所表的可能性反转过来。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of getting out of the way.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「让开、脱身」的意思。

items.example: The verb supplies the physical image of stepping aside.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「侧身避开」的具体意象。

items.example: The prefixed verb strengthens the act of avoidance.
items.exampleCN: 加前缀的动词强化了「避开」这一动作。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a statement about possibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成关于可能性的说法。

items.example: The adjective is the positive base that the negative prefix later blocks.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是肯定基形，随后被否定前缀挡住。

items.example: The negated adjective passes through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 带否定的形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

items.example: The noun names the quality that the adverb asserts.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名副词所断言的属性。

必然性

definition_zh: 地位；身份；状况；情形；职位
definition_en: the social, professional, or legal position of a person or thing at a time
core_image: 胸前别着的一枚徽章——别人一眼看出你站在哪一排
scene: 公司年会上，新头衔牌被摆上座位。 Her promotion gave her a new status in the company hierarchy.
sceneCN: 这里 status 是「地位；身份」（第 1 个义项：人在社会或组织中的位置）；句意为她的晋升使她在公司层级中获得了新地位。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加拉丁语成分构成的固定短语，义为「现状」
由本词加复合成分构成的短语，义为「身份的象征；彰显地位之物」

senses.title: A person's standing in society or an organization
senses.definition: the relative social or professional rank of a person
senses.definitionCN: 人在社会或职业中的相对等级
senses.example: Doctors enjoy high status in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在许多国家享有很高的地位。
senses.why: The badge pinned on the chest tells everyone which row you stand in.
senses.whyCN: 胸前的徽章告诉所有人你站在哪一排，即等级位置。

senses.title: The official condition of a person or thing in law or a system
senses.definition: the recognized legal or administrative condition of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或制度中被认可的法定情形
senses.example: The refugees were granted official status to stay.
senses.exampleCN: 这些难民获得了留居的正式身份。
senses.why: The badge issued by an office, not earned by crowds: a fixed registration.
senses.whyCN: 徽章不是靠人望挣来而是由机构颁发：一次固定登记。

senses.title: The current situation or condition at a given time
senses.definition: the present state of progress or affairs, as in status update
senses.definitionCN: 某事当前的进展或情形，如状态更新
senses.example: The pilot checked the status of all systems before takeoff.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员起飞前检查了所有系统的状态。
senses.why: A machine's badge is its row of indicator lights, read at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 机器的「徽章」是一排指示灯，一眼读出当前情形。

intro.en: Status is a straight borrowing of Latin status, the manner of standing, which also gave English state.
intro.cn: status 直接借自拉丁语 status（站立之姿），英语 state 亦同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root *sta- meant to stand.
items.cn: 重构词根 *sta- 意为「站立」。

items.en: Status, from the verb stare, meant the way one stands: condition and position.
items.cn: 拉丁语 status 源自动词 stare，指站立的方式：状况与位置。

items.en: In learned 17th-century usage, status meant legal condition, as in status in re publica.
items.cn: 17 世纪学术用语中，status 指法律身份。

items.en: English took status first for legal and diplomatic standing, later for social rank generally.
items.cn: 英语先用于法律与外交身份，后泛指社会地位。

items.en: Digital life added the sense of a system's current condition, as in status update.
items.cn: 数字时代增加了系统当前状态之义，如 status update。

note.en: Status is a Latin cousin of state and statute, and sits near different-root words for rank and condition.
note.cn: status 与 state、statute 是拉丁同源表亲，义场又靠近词源不同的等级、状况词。

entries.definition: a carved or cast figure that stands upright
entries.definitionCN: 雕像；与 status 同源于「站立」，只是拼读相近易混

entries.definition: a written law formally fixed
entries.definitionCN: 成文法令；同根词，原义「被立定之物」

entries.definition: a person's height or their moral importance
entries.definitionCN: 身高；声望；同根词，源自站立的高度

entries.definition: a position in a scale of importance or in an organization
entries.definitionCN: 等级；职级，强调序列中的位置

entries.definition: respect and admiration earned by success or quality
entries.definitionCN: 威望；声望，强调他人眼中的敬意

entries.definition: a person's reputation or official position
entries.definitionCN: 地位；名望，与 status 同含「站立」意象但词源路径不同

entries.definition: the physical state of something
entries.definitionCN: 状况；状态，偏重实体情况而非社会位置

normalIntro.en: Link status to its stand-root cousins and to real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 把 status 与「站立」词根表亲及真实固定短语关联起来。

normal.en: Latin stare means to stand; status is how one stands in a group.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，status 就是一人在群体中「立」的位置。

normal.en: Status quo is a Latin phrase meaning the existing situation.
normal.cn: status quo 是拉丁语短语，意为「现状」。

normal.en: Marital status appears on almost every official form.
normal.cn: marital status（婚姻状况）几乎出现在每张表格上。

normal.en: Status update is the standard name for posting your current state online.
normal.cn: status update 是发布个人当前状态的标准说法。

normal.en: Status, state, statue, and statute share the same stand-root.
normal.cn: status、state、statue、statute 共享同一「站立」词根。

abstract.en: Picture rows of people and a badge showing exactly which row is yours.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排人群，胸前徽章标出你属于哪一排。

abstract.en: See an airplane dashboard where each light reports a system's status.
abstract.cn: 看飞机仪表盘上每盏灯汇报一个系统的状态。

abstract.en: Feel the stillness of a statue standing, fixed where it was placed.
abstract.cn: 体会雕像静静立定、被固定在原处的静感。

examples.en: The new title raised her status within the team.
examples.cn: 新头衔提高了她在团队中的地位。

examples.en: Please indicate your marital status on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上注明婚姻状况。

examples.en: The app shows the status of your order in real time.
examples.cn: 应用会实时显示订单状态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯代特斯」——谐音「时代特设」：每个时代都特设一套身份地位。

root: 直接借自拉丁语 status（stare「站立」的派生名词），核心意象是「所立之位」；与 state、statue、statute 同根，词根一般认为可上溯至印欧语 *sta-（站立）。

sensesIntro.en: The standing-place image covers social rank, official registration, and a system's present reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 「所立之位」的意象涵盖社会等级、法定登记与系统的当前读数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a badge showing the row where someone stands
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚徽章，标出人站立的那一排

branches.en: social or professional rank
branches.cn: 社会或职业等级

branches.en: official legal or administrative standing
branches.cn: 法定或行政身份

branches.en: a system's current condition
branches.cn: 系统的当前状态

branches.en: the badge issued or earned
branches.cn: 挣来的或颁发的徽章

branches.en: a row of indicator lights read at a glance
branches.cn: 一眼读出的指示灯排

intro.en: Status belongs to the wide stand-root family, where every word fixes something in place.
intro.cn: status 属于庞大的「站立」词族，每个词都把某物固定在位置上。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare, to stand, produced status and its English cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare（站立）派生出 status 及其英语同族词。

items.structure: same root via Old French estat

items.meaning: a law set down in writing

items.structure: Latin phrase, the state in which

derivatives.zh: 由本词与拉丁语 quo 构成的固定短语，义为「现状」
由本词加复合成分构成的短语，义为「身份的象征；彰显地位之物」

definition_zh: 问题；议题；（报刊的）期号；（证券的）发行；发出；流出
definition_en: a subject people discuss or worry about, one set of printed copies, or the act of officially giving or sending something out
core_image: 水从闸门缝里涌出来，人群围住它讨论该怎么办
scene: 会议室的白板上写满条目，争论渐渐集中到同一行字上。 Everyone agreed the main issue was money.
sceneCN: 这里 issue 是「问题、议题」（第 1 个义项：需要讨论或解决的事），句意为大家都认为主要问题在于钱。画面里的物件：白板、条目、会议桌。

pos.zh: 名词：问题；议题；期号；发行

derivatives.zh: 由 issue 加 -ance 构成，义为「发行；签发」
由 issue 加 -er 构成，义为「发行人」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「已发行的；已签发的」

senses.title: A subject to discuss
senses.definition: an important topic that people are discussing or arguing about
senses.definitionCN: 人们正在讨论或争论的重要话题
senses.example: Housing is the biggest issue in this election.
senses.exampleCN: 住房是这次选举中最大的问题。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a going out or a flowing forth, and a disputed question is what flows out into public talk.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思有「流出」，而值得争论的问题正是从人群里流出来的话题。

senses.title: A problem to solve
senses.definition: a difficulty or problem that needs to be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理的困难或麻烦
senses.example: We have an issue with the water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的供水出了问题。
senses.why: A problem is a question that has begun to leak, so the outflow image turns into trouble.
senses.whyCN: 麻烦就是开始漏水的那个问题，流出的画面变成了故障。

senses.title: One set of printed copies
senses.definition: a single set of a newspaper or magazine published at one time
senses.definitionCN: 报纸或杂志一次出版的全部内容
senses.example: The May issue has a long article on bees.
senses.exampleCN: 五月那一期有一篇关于蜜蜂的长文。
senses.why: Each copy flows out from the press on one day, so the noun names one release.
senses.whyCN: 每一批印品在一天里从印刷机流出，于是这个名词指一次发行。

senses.title: To give out officially
senses.definition: to officially give something such as a document, ticket, or warning to people
senses.definitionCN: 正式把文件、票据或警告等交给别人
senses.example: The office issued new passes to all visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室向所有访客发出了新通行证。
senses.why: Issuing sends something out from an authority, exactly the going-out of the Latin source.
senses.whyCN: 签发是权威把东西送出去，正是词源里「向外走」的意思。

senses.title: To flow out
senses.definition: to come or flow out from a place or an opening
senses.definitionCN: 从某处、某开口流出来
senses.example: Water issued from a crack in the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 水从墙上的裂缝里流出。
senses.why: This is the oldest bodily sense, kept in modern technical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义，保留在现代技术性描述里。

senses.title: To result from
senses.definition: to come or result from a particular cause or source
senses.definitionCN: 由某个原因或来源产生
senses.example: Her doubts issue from an earlier failure.
senses.exampleCN: 她的疑虑源自更早的一次失败。
senses.why: Something that comes out of a source is the same movement as water out of a gap.
senses.whyCN: 从来源出来，与从缺口出水是同一种移动。

intro.en: Issue comes from Latin exire, "to go out", through its past participle exitus, "a going out".
intro.cn: issue 来自拉丁语 exire「出去」，经其过去分词 exitus「出去、出口」进入古法语。

items.en: exire meant to go out, from ex, out, and ire, to go.
items.cn: exire 意为出去，由 ex「向外」与 ire「走」组成。

items.en: exitus meant a going out, an end, or an outlet.
items.cn: exitus 意为出去、结果或出口。

items.en: Old French issue named an outlet, a way out, or a result.
items.cn: 古法语 issue 指出口、出路或结果。

items.en: English adopted issue for an exit and later for something sent out.
items.cn: 英语先以 issue 表示出口，后来表示送出的东西。

items.en: Printing made issue mean one release of a periodical, and the debate sense followed.
items.cn: 印刷出版让 issue 指一期刊物，讨论话题的义项随之出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the exit or issu- shape; the near-meaning group holds words for topics, problems, and sending out.
note.cn: 形近组共用 exit、issu- 形状；近义组收表示议题、问题与发出的词。

entries.definition: A way out or the act of leaving.
entries.definitionCN: 与 issue 同为拉丁 exire 的后代，义为「出口；离开」。

entries.definition: The act of officially issuing something.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ance 构成，义为「发行；签发」。

entries.definition: The material of which body parts are made.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「组织」，拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The subject of a talk or text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「主题」，偏中性的讨论对象。

entries.definition: A difficulty that needs solving.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「难题」，比 issue 更直接。

entries.definition: To give things out to many people.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「分发」，与 issue 的发出义相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the Latin going-out verb to magazines, tickets, and arguments.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语「出去」的动词走到杂志、票据与争论。

normal.en: Latin exire means to go out.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 exire 意为出去。

normal.en: exitus means a going out or an outlet.
normal.cn: exitus 意为出去或出口。

normal.en: An issue of a magazine goes out on one day.
normal.cn: 一期杂志在一天里发行出去。

normal.en: To issue a ticket is to hand it out officially.
normal.cn: issue a ticket 就是正式发出票据。

normal.en: The main issue is what everyone argues about.
normal.cn: main issue 就是大家都在争的那件事。

abstract.en: An issue is a subject that leaks out of a group.
abstract.cn: 议题是从人群里漏出来的话题。

abstract.en: A problem is an issue with its lid off.
abstract.cn: 麻烦是揭了盖子的议题。

abstract.en: What issues from a source was inside it before.
abstract.cn: 从来源流出的东西，原本就在里面。

examples.en: Privacy is a serious issue for many users.
examples.cn: 隐私对许多用户来说是严重的问题。

examples.en: The bank will issue a new card next week.
examples.cn: 银行下周会发行一张新卡。

root: 拉丁语 exire「出去」（ex 向外 + ire 走）→ exitus「出去；出口」→ 古法语 issue → 英语 issue。同族有 exit、issuance、issuer。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a topic under discussion, a difficulty, one release of a periodical, official giving out, flowing out, and resulting from.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：讨论的议题、麻烦、一期刊物、正式发出、流出，以及出自某来源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water slipping out of a gate while a crowd argues about it.
core.cn: 核心意象：水从闸门缝里涌出，人群围着它争论。

branches.en: THE ELECTION: one topic everyone keeps returning to.
branches.cn: 选举这条线：人人反复回到的那个话题。

branches.en: THE PIPE: a leak that has become trouble.
branches.cn: 水管这条线：漏成了麻烦。

branches.en: THE BEES: one month of a magazine leaving the press.
branches.cn: 蜜蜂这条线：从印刷机出来的一期杂志。

branches.en: THE PASS: a document handed out at a desk.
branches.cn: 通行证这条线：在窗口发出去的文件。

branches.en: THE CRACK: water out of a gap, doubt out of a failure.
branches.cn: 裂缝这条线：水从缺口出，疑虑从失败出。

intro.en: Issue is a French reshaping of the Latin noun exitus; only English endings are later additions.
intro.cn: issue 是古法语对拉丁名词 exitus 的改写，后面加的英语词尾是后来才有的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all turn on ex-, out, and ire, to go.
latinIntro.cn: 这些拉丁同族词都围绕 ex-「向外」与 ire「走」。

items.example: Combined with ire it forms exire.
items.exampleCN: 与 ire 结合构成 exire。

items.example: The base verb of the family.

items.exampleCN: 法语写作 issue，而非 exite。

items.example: It forms issue date and issue number.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 issue date 与 issue number。

intro.en: Holy is an old English word for something set apart for God.
intro.cn: holy 是古英语词，指为神而分别出来、归于神圣的事物。

items.en: Hailag meant holy or whole.
items.cn: hailag 意为神圣的、完整的。

items.en: Halig meant holy.
items.cn: halig 意为神圣的。

items.en: Holi kept the religious sense.
items.cn: holi 保留了宗教含义。

items.cn: holy 用来描述地点、日子和人。

items.cn: holiday 由 holy day 演变而来。

normalIntro.en: Holy describes what people set apart for God.
normalIntro.cn: holy 描述人们为神而分别出来、格外敬重的事物。

normal.en: This old temple is considered holy.
normal.cn: 这座古庙被认为是神圣的。

normal.en: Pilgrims walked slowly across the holy ground.
normal.cn: 朝圣者慢慢走过圣地。

normal.en: The holy book is read every morning.

normal.en: Sunday was once a holy day for the village.

abstract.en: Holy is a word for what is set apart, not for what is merely old.

abstract.en: A holy place asks people to lower their voices.
abstract.cn: 神圣之地会让人放低声音。

abstract.en: What we treat as holy shows what we worship.
